articles.title: Chuva em Cosmópolis causa alagamentos, queda de árvore e atola carro | G1
articles.standfirst: Transtornos foram registrados durante as chuvas que atingiram a cidade nesta sexta (13). Prefeitura informou que acompanha
articles.summary: Chuva em Cosmópolis causa queda de árvores, granizo e alagamentos; na Rua Francisco Cezário, um carro afundou em um buraco devido à força da enxurrada na sexta-feira.
articles.body:
Cosmópolis (SP) registrou, ao menos, quatro ocorrências de transtornos provocados pelas fortes chuvas que atingiram a região na sexta-feira (13), incluindo queda de uma árvore, alagamento de residência e pontos de enxurrada em diferentes bairros da cidade. Assista no vídeo acima e veja locais, na reportagem.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Cosmópolis, o bairro Santo Antônio registrou grande fluxo de água, mas a situação foi controlada. Os bairros Paineiras/Baguá e Rosamélia também tiveram pontos de atenção por causa do volume intenso de chuva.

Apesar disso, a administração municipal informou que não havia risco iminente nas áreas afetadas.

Temporal em Cosmópolis provoca enxurradas, queda de granizo e deixa carro atolado; veja locais — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Por causa da força da chuva, uma residência no Jardim das Paineiras foi invadida pela água. De acordo com a prefeitura, o imóvel já havia sido atingido por outro temporal, quando um muro foi derrubado.

As secretarias municipais de Segurança Pública e de Promoção Social atuaram no atendimento aos moradores afetados, prestando apoio e assistência às famílias atingidas.

Uma moradora da Rua Francisco Cezário registrou o momento em que um carro afundou em um trecho da via com buracos. Segundo ela, o veículo estava no local para passar por um reparo mecânico.

A moradora relatou que a rua apresentava diversos buracos e que havia areia espalhada pela via.

Moradores dos bairros Chácara Santo Antônio e Jardim das Paineiras registraram momentos em que a água invadiu casas durante a chuva.

Por causa da força da enxurrada e do grande volume de água, a correnteza formou uma espécie de cascata que escoava dos imóveis para a rua.

Moradores dos bairros Jardim de Fáveri, Santana, Taillon e Parque Residencial das Andorinhas também registraram chuva de granizo durante o temporal.

Sobre os transtornos relatados por moradores na Rua Aquilino Tescari, na Chácara Santo Antônio, a prefeitura informou que:

"[Plano de obras] encontra-se em fase de licitação emergencial para viabilizar as intervenções necessárias no local, com o objetivo de minimizar os riscos de novos alagamentos e garantir mais segurança aos moradores", declarou a prefeitura em nota à EPTV , afiliada da Globo para Piracicaba e região.

articles.title: EUA propõem que Ucrânia ceda território à Rússia em troca de entrada na Otan, diz Zelensky | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente ucraniano afirma que Washington levantou a possibilidade de um acordo envolvendo a região de Donbas, mas rejeita abrir mão de território e alerta para os riscos de enfraquecimento da Otan.
articles.summary: Presidente ucraniano afirma que Washington levantou a possibilidade de um acordo envolvendo a região de Donbas, mas rejeita abrir mão de território.
articles.body:
O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelensky, durante entrevista coletiva em cúpula de líderes da União Europeia, em Bruxelas, na Bélgica, em 16 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Yves Herman/Reuters

O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelensky , afirmou que os Estados Unidos levantaram, pela primeira vez, a possibilidade de o país retirar suas tropas das áreas de Donbas, no leste ucraniano, que ainda não estão sob controle russo, em troca da adesão à Organização do Tratado do Atlântico Norte ( Otan ).

Zelensky, no entanto, reiterou que Kiev não abrirá mão de seu território e alertou que Moscou pode aproveitar as negociações para enfraquecer a Otan e tentar alterar as fronteiras da Europa.

Segundo o presidente ucraniano, os EUA também levantaram a possibilidade de criar uma nova estrutura de segurança para o continente como parte dos esforços para encerrar a guerra com a Rússia.

"Na minha opinião, isso pode ser perigoso", disse Zelensky a jornalistas na sexta-feira (13), ao comentar a proposta. "Essa não deveria ser a pauta principal." As declarações só puderam ser divulgadas neste sábado (14).

Segundo Zelensky, Moscou estaria mais interessada em rediscutir a segurança europeia do que em concentrar os esforços no fim da guerra, que já dura quatro anos e meio.

"O desejo de Putin [presidente russo] de alterar as fronteiras na Europa é um fato. Tenho certeza de que isso faz parte de seu plano de revisão das garantias de segurança na Europa", afirmou. "Isso é perigoso porque, na minha opinião, são justamente coisas como essa que levam a guerras ou à escalada de conflitos."

Líderes europeus têm defendido que as decisões sobre a segurança do continente sejam tomadas pelos próprios países da região.

Eles também alertam para o risco de permitir que a Rússia determine as condições de uma nova estrutura de segurança ou negocie o futuro da Otan.

Zelensky afirmou que a Ucrânia negocia com seus aliados um amplo pacote de segurança, que pode incluir garantias específicas da Otan e da União Europeia, o fortalecimento das Forças Armadas ucranianas e apoio financeiro por um período determinado. A proposta também prevê um plano de reconstrução do país.

"Se os americanos nos confirmarem exatamente isso, juntamente com outros parceiros da Otan, perguntarei à sociedade ucraniana o que ela pensa: aceitamos ou não?", disse Zelensky.

O presidente ressaltou que qualquer acordo não significaria reconhecer como russos os territórios ucranianos ocupados por Moscou.

Zelensky também descartou a possibilidade de a Ucrânia assumir uma posição de neutralidade, argumentando que isso exigiria uma mudança na Constituição do país.

"Se Putin espera que a neutralidade da Ucrânia seja estabelecida, isso não vai acontecer", afirmou. "De qualquer forma, não fazemos parte da Otan atualmente."

Ucrânia ataca instalação petrolífera na Rússia

Em outra frente do conflito, as forças ucranianas atacaram uma importante instalação petrolífera russa que abastece o esforço de guerra de Moscou, segundo comunicado divulgado neste sábado pelo Estado-Maior da Ucrânia.

Ataques ucranianos atingiram, na sexta-feira (13), uma estação de oleoduto próxima à vila de Prosvet, na região russa de Samara, e provocaram incêndios em vários tanques de armazenamento de petróleo, segundo os militares ucranianos. Moscou não comentou o ataque.

Segundo o Estado-Maior da Ucrânia, a instalação tem papel importante na rede de exportação de petróleo da Rússia para o mercado internacional.

Os militares também informaram que suas forças atacaram o aeródromo de Lipetsk-2, na região russa de Lipetsk.

Zelensky defende que Europa decida seu próprio futuro

Zelensky alertou que discussões mais amplas sobre a segurança europeia poderiam abrir espaço para Putin exigir mudanças na presença militar da Otan no continente, incluindo a retirada de tropas americanas.

Segundo o presidente ucraniano, Putin já havia apresentado propostas semelhantes ao então presidente dos Estados Unidos, Joe Biden, em 2021, com o objetivo de alterar a distribuição de poder na Europa e no mundo.

"Acho que Putin vai mencionar a Finlândia e a Suécia. Tenho certeza de que ele vai levantar a questão da Hungria e da presença de tropas americanas nos países bálticos", afirmou Zelensky.

Para o presidente, qualquer mudança nos acordos de segurança europeus deve ser decidida pelos países europeus que integram a Otan, e somente depois do fim da guerra na Ucrânia.

"A sequência deve ser a seguinte: um cessar-fogo, o fim da guerra na Ucrânia e garantias de segurança para a Ucrânia", afirmou. "Não pode haver garantias de segurança na Europa, ou para a Europa, sem a Ucrânia."

Cessar-fogo no setor energético e troca de prisioneiros são prioridades

Equipes de resgate buscam vítimas de ataque aéreo russo em escola subterrânea que servia como centro de distribuição humanitária em Zaporizhzhia, na Ucrânia, em 2 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Stringer

Zelensky afirmou que as prioridades da Ucrânia nas negociações em Abu Dhabi incluem a suspensão de ataques contra instalações de energia, a reabertura do Mar Negro, a libertação de prisioneiros e a preparação de um encontro entre os líderes dos países para tentar encerrar a guerra.

Segundo ele, os representantes russos não tinham autorização para tomar decisões sobre várias questões discutidas nas reuniões.

Zelensky também afirmou que Moscou não demonstrou disposição para aceitar um acordo de suspensão dos ataques ao setor energético.

"Na reunião em Abu Dhabi, a delegação russa disse que não tinha autorização para decidir sobre essa questão, mas também podemos ver que eles não estão dispostos a fazê-lo", afirmou. Segundo Zelensky, os negociadores foram orientados a tratar diretamente com Putin das questões relacionadas ao cessar-fogo.

O presidente ucraniano também afirmou que conversas realizadas em Moscou com negociadores americanos resultaram em um acordo para a troca de mais de mil prisioneiros de cada lado.

O número exato ainda estava em discussão, mas a estimativa era de 1.200 a 1.300 pessoas por país .

Zelensky disse ainda que Washington apoiava a exigência ucraniana de incluir representantes europeus diretamente nas próximas negociações, em vez de deixá-los fora das principais reuniões.

🔎 Segundo ele, Reino Unido, França, Alemanha e Itália estavam entre os países representados nos encontros em Abu Dhabi. A expectativa é que entre três e cinco representantes europeus participem das próximas discussões.

Zelensky questiona restrições ao Starshield

Zelensky acusou a SpaceX de impor restrições ao funcionamento do sistema de satélites Starshield em territórios ucranianos ocupados pela Rússia. Segundo ele, as limitações têm dificultado a interceptação de drones russos.

O presidente afirmou que a velocidade permitida pelo sistema foi limitada a 161 km/h nas áreas ocupadas e que as restrições estavam em vigor havia cinco dias.

Zelensky questionou a explicação de que o problema seria técnico. Segundo ele, as limitações parecem ter sido impostas pela própria SpaceX, apesar das garantias anteriores do secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio, de que o Starshield estava mais diretamente sob controle do governo dos Estados Unidos.

"As restrições atuais do Starshield sugerem que a SpaceX as impôs", afirmou Zelensky. "É o que nossa equipe está me dizendo. Portanto, isso não coincide com o que ouvimos antes. É por isso que precisamos esclarecer tudo isso."

Segundo o presidente, as limitações impedem as forças ucranianas de interceptar drones russos Shahed, equipados com motores a jato, enquanto sobrevoam os territórios ocupados.

Com isso, os militares precisam esperar até que os equipamentos alcancem áreas onde as restrições não se aplicam.

articles.title: Tánaiste asks politicians for feedback on Irish unity 'blueprint'
articles.summary: Simon Harris' party Fine Gael published proposals on how to prepare for Irish unity last week.
articles.body:
The tánaiste (Irish deputy prime minister) has asked some political parties in Northern Ireland and the republic for feedback on his party's so-called "blueprint" on Irish unity.

Simon Harris' party Fine Gael published proposals on how to prepare for Irish unity last week. He has now asked some party leaders in Northern Ireland for their views, including unionist parties.

It comes days after the taoiseach (Irish prime minister), leader of Fianna Fáil, circulated a document to his parliamentary party laying out his own thoughts on how to prepare for a united Ireland .

Among their proposals, Fine Gael has suggested appointing a junior minister in the Irish government for "north south relations".

The party also published a document by an economist who works as an adviser to Harris, where it was suggested that the first-year cost of reunification ranges from about €3bn (£2.5bn) to €25bn (£20.8) to the Irish exchequer.

Harris has asked for "views" on the plans as well as areas where there may be a need for "further consideration".

In a letter accompanying the proposals, he said: "No one political party owns the discussion about the future of this island, nor should any one party seek to determine its outcome.

"That is why I believe this must be an inclusive conversation, informed by evidence, respectful of different constitutional perspectives and grounded firmly in the Good Friday Agreement and the principle of consent," he wrote.

The party leaders who have been sent the letter in Northern Ireland are: Democratic Unionist Party leader (DUP) Gavin Robinson, Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) leader Jon Burrows, Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) leader Claire Hanna, Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV) leader Jim Allister and Alliance leader Naomi Long.

The party leaders who were sent the letter in the republic are: the taoiseach, Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald, Aontú leader Peadar Tóibín, Labour party leader Ivana Bacik, Social Democrat acting leader Cian O'Callaghan, Independent Ireland leader Michael Collins, Green Party leader Roderic O'Gorman and Richard Boyd-Barrett of People Before Profit.

"There will be differing views and difficult conversations, but complexity cannot become an excuse for inaction," wrote Harris.

"I would very much welcome your views on the proposals and the wider issues raised, including areas where we might identify common ground or where further consideration is required.

"I am writing to all major political parties across this island - I hope you will receive this report in the constructive and respectful spirit in which it is intended," he wrote in the letter, seen by BBC News NI.

articles.title: The Trump administration has proposed selling parts of America's federal land holdings to states, tribes and local governments under a new five-year plan, but has not identified which parcels could be sold
articles.summary: America's vast public landscapes, long regarded as a shared national inheritance, are once again at the centre of a political battle over who should
articles.body: America's vast public landscapes, long regarded as a shared national inheritance, are once again at the centre of a political battle over who should control the country's natural resources. President Donald Trump's administration has outlined a proposal that could reshape the future of federally managed land, opening the door to sales and transfers to states, tribal governments and local authorities. While officials have presented the move as an effort to improve efficiency and redirect resources towards conservation, the absence of clearly identified properties and disposal criteria has raised concerns among conservationists, outdoor enthusiasts and lawmakers.A new direction for federal land managementAccording to The Washington Post, the proposal forms part of a five-year strategic plan released by the Department of the Interior, outlining the agency's priorities for fiscal years 2026 through 2030. The 28-page document identifies four central objectives, including reducing the size of the federal estate by offering certain properties for purchase to states, local governments and tribes.The department has argued that disposing of lands considered less nationally significant would allow it to concentrate resources on properties of greater federal importance. However, neither the specific parcels under consideration nor the geographical scope of potential sales has been disclosed. The administration has also not explained what qualifies a property as nationally significant, the report adds.According to The Washington Post, the Interior Department oversees more than 750,000 square miles of land, an area larger than Texas and California combined, alongside extensive underground mineral resources. Much of this estate is concentrated in Western states, where federal ownership remains particularly substantial. Nevada, for instance, has nearly 80 per cent of its territory under federal control.Under the proposed arrangement, some proceeds from land sales would be returned to purchasing entities for conservation initiatives elsewhere, potentially supporting improved recreational access while reducing the government's long-term management expenses.Conservationists raise access concernsThe proposal has drawn criticism from outdoor recreation groups concerned that transferring federal properties to state authorities could eventually restrict public access. Outdoor Life reports that hunting and fishing advocates are particularly worried about losing access to lesser-known Bureau of Land Management properties that remain important recreational destinations.The distinction between federal and state ownership is significant. State-managed properties often operate under different access regulations, with restrictions on camping, driving and recreational activities. Consequently, a transfer could make certain landscapes less accessible even if they remain publicly owned.Outdoor Life also highlights concerns about the department's proposed workforce consolidation. The strategic plan promises further reductions across federal agencies, including the National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management and US Fish and Wildlife Service. These organizations have long struggled with staff and funding, raising concerns about their ability to meet current needs.The only areas identified for potential staffing expansion are law enforcement and public safety, rather than conservation operations.Legal, political oppositionBipartisan opposition exists to the proposal. The former Trump interior secretary told The Washington Post that Ryan Zinke still opposes selling public lands. He has indicated that he would vote against legislation advancing such a move.Democratic lawmakers have also pledged to resist the initiative, arguing that federally owned landscapes should remain protected from commercial interests. Their opposition follows earlier unsuccessful attempts by some Western lawmakers to sell large portions of federal land, including a proposal by Utah Republican Senator Mike Lee involving more than two million acres.Legal restrictions could present another obstacle. Natural resources law professor Mark Squillace told The Washington Post that federal legislation places significant limits on property disposals. Protected lands cannot simply be sold, while other parcels must satisfy specific requirements, such as being uneconomical to manage or supporting important public objectives, including community expansion and economic development.Wider changes to public land policyThe strategic plan extends beyond property sales. Outdoor Life reports that it also prioritises domestic energy production, critical mineral development, artificial intelligence infrastructure and a major restructuring of federal wildfire management through a new US Wildland Fire Service.Separately, the Bureau of Land Management has proposed changes to its resource management planning process. The proposed rule would eliminate the existing 90-day public comment period for major plans and remove the requirement to release draft plans for public feedback, potentially replacing these processes with public meetings. The proposal remains open for public comments until January 11, 2027.These changes could have considerable implications because BLM resource management plans help determine where activities such as mining, drilling and grazing are permitted, as well as which properties may be considered for disposal.Although the five-year strategy establishes the administration's direction, it does not guarantee that the proposed land transfers will happen. Congressional approval and existing federal protections remain important considerations. For now, with no specific parcels identified, the proposal has opened a wider debate about whether America's public lands should primarily serve economic development, conservation or the millions of people who rely on them for recreation.Images Courtesy: istock and InstagramYou use AI every day. articles.title: Over 2,000 involved: Russia-Ukraine set for biggest-ever prisoner swap amid Trump-led diplomacy

articles.body: Ukraine is expecting what could become the largest prisoner exchange with Russia since the beginning of the war, with more than 1,000 people from each side likely to be released as Washington steps up diplomatic efforts to bring an end to the conflict.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Friday that Kyiv was taking seriously assurances from its American partners that the proposed exchange would be the biggest of the war. More than a thousand people from each side," Zelenskyy said in a post on X.He said the proposed exchange was particularly important for thousands of Ukrainian families waiting for the return of their relatives and that he expected a report on the preparations shortly.The proposed exchange comes amid renewed diplomatic efforts led by the United States to end the Russia-Ukraine war.US President Donald Trump's special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have held separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelenskyy in an effort to advance negotiations.The US envoys met Putin in Moscow before holding discussions with Zelenskyy in Ireland on November 13. The meeting with the Ukrainian President focused on the next steps towards ending the conflict and establishing security guarantees for Kyiv.The discussions with Putin also covered humanitarian cooperation, including preparations for a prisoner exchange. Zelenskyy said Kyiv had agreed with the American envoys on the next steps, expressing hope that Washington and Ukraine would work together towards a lasting peace.Apart from the proposed prisoner exchange, Zelenskyy highlighted the outcomes of his recent diplomatic engagements with European leaders, including a defence assistance package worth 645 million euros from Denmark.The package will include additional ammunition for F-16 fighter jets and energy assistance for Ukraine. articles.title: What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices?
articles.summary: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
articles.body:
Mention Christmas markets these days and the conversation often turns to rising prices – from £8 bratwursts, £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps and even £5 for a few marshmallow sticks.

But what do the people behind the stalls think? Are they benefiting from the hikes or are their own profits being squeezed?

Traders at Manchester's Christmas markets told the BBC they were feeling the pressure of increasing bills for staff, ingredients and energy, with some saying they were making less money despite charging more.

One trader said it costs at least £4,000 a day to run each her four stalls, while another has cut prices to keep customers coming back.

Nils Borstel, 25, helps run Bratwurst King, a family business which has operated at the markets since 1999.

He said a sausage that previously cost £3.50 now sold for £8, with much of the increase taking place over the past five or six years.

"But we don't earn more money," he said.

Borstel, whose family operates four stalls across the city centre, said rising costs for meat, electricity, staffing and accommodation had forced the business to increase prices.

About 15 workers travel from Germany to help run the stalls, alongside staff recruited in the UK.

He said that despite busy crowds and dry weather during the opening weekend, people appeared more cautious about spending than in previous years.

For example, some customers were now buying one portion of food to share, rather than purchasing one each, he said.

Borstel said he had seen a change in spending habits since 2019, when customers were more willing to buy food and drinks without worrying about the cost.

He acknowledged that prices were high and did not want to increase them, but said the they were necessary to cover expenses.

Among those questioning the costs were Neve and Poppy, both 18.

Neve, a student, said she had spent about £15 on one dish, while Poppy, who is taking a gap year, paid £11 for a Yorkshire pudding wrap.

"I think it was pricey for what it was," Neve said.

Poppy also felt she had not received much food for the money, although said it was tasty.

Both said they enjoyed going into the city and looking around the markets, while Neve sympathised with traders, saying she thought the cost of renting space could force businesses to raise prices.

Charlotte Whittle, director of CT Catering, has been trading at the markets for 10 years and now operates four stalls.

She said each stall cost at least £1,000 a day to run, bringing her total daily operating costs to at least £4,000.

Whittle, who employs a range of staff, said customers often underestimated the work and expense involved.

Before the markets opened, her business spent two weeks preparing its stalls, with another two weeks needed to dismantle them after Christmas.

She said the costs included staff wages, accommodation, deliveries, storage, packaging and card payment fees.

Parking three vans in Manchester city centre could cost £100 a day alone, she said, with the vehicles needed to replenish stock throughout busy trading periods.

"They think that you're just selling cookies," she said.

Whittle, who began her business selling homemade cakes at street food markets, said the cost of stock and packaging had increased significantly over the years.

Although she had increased some prices, she said she had chosen to absorb part of those costs rather than risk putting customers off.

"We've had to take a massive cut on profits," she said.

She also argued that the standard of street food had improved and customers were receiving food comparable in quality to that served in restaurants.

But not every trader has responded to rising costs by putting up prices.

Clark Murphy, whose family has traded at the markets for 22 years, runs Mr Crimble Crumble, which sells fruit crumbles from two stalls.

He said the business had kept most prices unchanged for three years and had reduced the cost of its largest portion by £2.

Murphy said cooking oil and biodegradable packaging had become more expensive, but the business wanted to retain customers who returned each Christmas.

"We haven't increased our prices for three years now," he said.

He said the business remained profitable, although margins were under pressure and card payments added to operating costs.

At another food stall, a notice offered customers £1 off each drink or dish when paying cash.

"Card fees are crazy – help us keep it simple," it said.

Meanwhile, a gift trader calling himself Ernie the Elf, who sells handmade Christmas decorations in Albert Square, said visitors could still find affordable products.

His decorations cost £4 each or three for £10, while metal signs were priced at £9.

Ernie, who is in his second year at the Manchester markets, said traders faced substantial expenses, including accommodation and parking.

But he believed the markets offered good value, pointing out that people could enjoy the festive atmosphere without having to spend money.

Tyler, from Australia, and Rebecca, from Hong Kong, were enjoying their first Christmas in England with their daughter.

Rebecca bought four brownies for £10, while Tyler paid £6 for a meat pie, which he said was not unreasonable compared with some other prices.

However, he described another stall charging £5 for three marshmallow sticks as "outrageous".

The couple said the markets were part of enjoying their first Christmas in England with their daughter.

Despite questioning the cost of some products, Tyler said the experience was worthwhile.

"I think if you don't buy anything, it's still great to come," he said.

articles.title: Gardeners across Sussex hedging their bets in face of extreme weather
articles.summary: Gardeners across Sussex are changing their planting strategies after this year's unprecedented heat.
articles.body:
Gardeners in one of the most drought-hit parts of the UK have said they are adapting their planting strategies amid increasingly extreme weather.

West Sussex - like most of the country - experienced an unprecedented summer marked by record-breaking heatwaves and severe drought.

The conditions have put immense stress on many traditional plant species, with some seriously struggling or dying completely.

Iain Parkinson, head of landscape and horticulture at Kew Wakehurst near Ardingly, said he had seen a "big change" in climate over the some 40 years he has worked there.

Meanwhile, senior gardener at High Beeches near Haywards Heath, Elliot Chandler, said some rhododendrons had died off this year.

"That's probably going to continue," he said.

"We'll do what we can for the plants...but if they're not surviving, then we need to plant different things.

"That's the only way we can really maintain the garden and keep it full of interest and flowers."

Joe Whelan, head gardener at Nymans in Handcross, warned another year of drought could be "quite detrimental" on larger, more mature trees.

The gardeners said planting a greater diversity of species will be key to climate resilience, with plants from North America, southeastern Europe, central Asia, South Korea and Japan potentially faring better in future.

Chandler added it will not be a case of ripping out old plants and planting new species "in one go" but rather a gradual change over time with a "really diverse mix of things".

Whelan said it will be difficult to predict what will do well in the future.

It will be about "experimenting and accepting that some things probably aren't going to make it", he continued.

articles.title: Woman feels 'lucky to be alive' after weight-loss jabs ordeal
articles.summary: Kay Roscoe was rushed to hospital after taking what she thought was the weight-loss drug retatrutide.
articles.body:
A woman has described how she could not speak or stand before being rushed to hospital after taking an unlicensed weight-loss jab.

Kay Roscoe, 38, from Birkenhead, said she had used a substance sold as retatrutide, or "reta", for two months before falling seriously ill.

The experimental drug is not approved for general use and is available only through clinical trials. Products claiming to contain it are widely sold online, but it is not known whether Kay took genuine retatrutide.

She is now warning others about the risks. "I am the luckiest person to be alive. Honestly I can't say it enough, get off the pens," she said.

On the day of her collapse, Kay had been due to go out for a roast dinner with a friend.

When she failed to answer her phone, her friend went to check on her at home and found her unable to speak or stand.

"I was frothing at the mouth, not responsive at all," she said, recounting what her friend later told her. "My eyes were moving around, but I couldn't speak or move or do anything."

Kay, who has no memory of the episode, said her friends rang an ambulance and told paramedics she had been taking "reta" before she was rushed to hospital.

She said it took more than an hour for her to regain consciousness.

Hospital tests confirmed Kay had suffered severe hypoglycaemia, a condition where blood sugar falls to dangerously low levels.

Medical records attributed the episode to an unlicensed weight-loss injection.

Kay said doctors warned her she could have died if her friend had found her just half an hour later.

In the weeks since, Kay said she has continued to suffer health problems, including extreme fatigue.

She said further tests had shown she had signs of liver damage and high cholesterol, neither of which she had before the episode. .

"I don't drink very much, I don't smoke," she said. "I've never had a problem with anything like this. I just feel run down and drained. My body feels all over the place."

Kay had started injecting herself with the substance about two months earlier.

A former regular gym-goer, she said she was attracted to the prospect of quicker weight loss after seeing posts on social media.

"Going to the gym takes longer. I saw my friends on it and saw them losing weight. And I thought, everyone is taking it and they've all been fine, so I'll try it. I didn't really read into the licensing," she said.

Kay bought the jab from a friend and said she believed it was legitimate after scanning a QR code on the pen, which took her to what appeared to be a pharmaceutical website.

Initially, she was pleased with the results, saying she lost a "drastic amount" of weight within weeks. But the injections had also significantly reduced her appetite.

"I was made up with the change, but I was never hungry," she said.

In the days leading up to her hospital admission, Kay said she had eaten very little.

Retatrutide is being developed by pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly as a potential treatment for obesity.

Unlike existing weight-loss drugs, such as Wegovy and Mounjaro, which target one or two hormone receptors, retatrutide acts on three, earning it the nickname "triple G".

The drug is still undergoing clinical trials, with Eli Lilly planning to apply for approval in the US early next year.

Eli Lilly said retatrutide had not been approved by any regulator and could not legally be sold for human use.

A spokesperson said: "Counterfeit and black market medicines are unverified, unregulated and potentially dangerous - in some cases, deadly."

The company said it was working with the UK's medicines regulator, the MHRA, police and social media platforms to remove illegal products.

"Stronger, coordinated law enforcement must be sustained to protect UK patients from unsafe fake medicines," the spokesperson added.

Dr Nas Khattak, a research doctor based in Chester who has worked on clinical trials of weight-loss drugs, warned of the dangers of injections obtained through unregulated sources.

"You cannot verify the dose, purity, sterility, or even the contents," he said.

"If something goes wrong there is no proper medical oversight."

Dr Khattak said he had seen substances advertised through messaging apps, bodybuilding forums and private sellers, with users openly sharing dosing advice and supplier recommendations.

He said he had also encountered serious complications during his NHS hospital work, including a young woman who required intensive care after taking a weight-loss injection obtained from a beautician. He said it was never established exactly what substance she had taken.

"It really does feel like a roll of the dice," he said.

The UK's medicines regulator, the MHRA, has seized products claiming to contain retatrutide and says it is working to disrupt their illegal importation and distribution.

What symptoms should people look out for?

Dr Khattak said common side effects of weight-loss injections included mild nausea, feeling full more quickly, constipation and tiredness.

He said headaches, dizziness, a dry mouth and very dark urine could be signs of dehydration and should prompt medical advice.

However, he warned people to seek urgent medical attention if they experienced more serious symptoms, including:

Since sharing her story on Facebook, Kay said she had received messages from about 100 people describing their own experiences with weight-loss injections.

"You never think anything's going to happen to you. But we all do things because we want to lose weight," she said. "You see a new thing on the market and want to try it. I just think it's very dangerous."

Kay also revealed the impact her ordeal has had on her family.

"They've gone mad at me and warned me not to take it. They said, 'There's nothing of you', but you don't see yourself like that, do you?"

She now plans to return to the gym and eat healthily.

"Please, everyone, stop taking a needle to be skinny. Imagine not waking up, like I nearly didn't. And then my poor family losing someone over taking something you didn't even know what it was."

articles.title: Psychology says people who repeatedly check door locks, taps and switches even after leaving may not trust their memory enough to feel reassured
articles.summary: You are halfway down the stairs when a thought suddenly crosses your mind: Did I turn off the bathroom tap?
articles.body: You are halfway down the stairs when a thought suddenly crosses your mind: Did I turn off the bathroom tap? You remember closing it, but you are not completely sure. You go back, check it and leave again.A few minutes later, another doubt appears. Was the front door properly locked? You may have checked it before leaving, but now you feel the need to return and try the handle once more.For some people, this happens regularly. They check the taps, switches, gas knobs and door locks before leaving home, yet the reassurance does not always last. Even after confirming that everything is in order, they may find themselves questioning whether they checked properly.Psychology offers one possible explanation: repeated checking can be connected to uncertainty and reduced confidence in one's own memory. In some cases, the more a person checks, the less certain they may feel.Why checking something again may make you trust your memory lessA 2023 systematic review titled ‘Memory confidence and memory accuracy deterioration following repeated checking’ examined 29 studies involving 2,180 participants. The researchers found that repeated checking was associated with a substantial decline in memory confidence, while its effect on actual memory accuracy was much smaller. In simple terms, people may become less confident that they remember performing an action correctly, even when their memory of what happened has not deteriorated to the same extent.This could help explain why someone who has already checked a locked door might still feel uncertain a few minutes later. They may remember turning the key, but the memory does not feel convincing enough to stop the doubt.The review also noted that the findings came largely from experimental studies and may not fully represent everyone who experiences compulsive checking in everyday life.The more you check, the less reassured you may feelAn earlier experiment published in Behaviour Research and Therapy in 2006 examined this pattern using ordinary household objects. Researchers asked 50 undergraduate students to repeatedly switch a real kitchen stove on and off and check it, or perform a similar repeated checking task involving a kitchen tap.After 19 checking trials, participants who repeatedly checked the stove reported lower confidence in their memory, along with less vividness and detail when recalling the action. The researchers found that repeatedly checking an action could make people less certain about their memory of having performed it.A person may not be forgetting whether they turned off the switch or closed the tap. Instead, they may be finding it increasingly difficult to trust the memory of having done so.When does this become more than an ordinary safety check?Checking the front door before leaving home or making sure the gas is switched off is sensible. Most people occasionally return to verify something when they are distracted, tired or unsure whether they completed an action. The concern arises when checking becomes repetitive, distressing or difficult to resist, even after the person knows that the task has already been completed.A 2020 meta-analysis titled ‘Why check? A meta-analysis of checking in obsessive-compulsive disorder: Threat vs. distrust of senses’ examined 22 studies comparing 663 people with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and 614 healthy controls.The researchers found greater checking among people with OCD during perceptual tasks. Their findings also supported the role of uncertainty and distrust of one's senses in compulsive checking.Repeated checking is a recognised compulsion associated with OCD, but checking a door twice or returning to turn off a tap does not, by itself, mean someone has the condition.What can help when checking becomes repetitive?If you recognise this pattern, it may help to notice when a reasonable safety check turns into repeated reassurance-seeking.Complete one deliberate check: Pay attention while turning off the tap, switching off the appliance or locking the door instead of doing it automatically while distracted.Avoid rushing through the routine: A moment of attention can make it easier to remember completing the action.Notice the difference between a real concern and a recurring doubt: Ask yourself whether there is new information or whether the same uncertainty has returned.Seek professional help if it affects daily life: If checking takes up significant time, causes distress or makes you repeatedly return home, a mental health professional can help assess what is happening. Cognitive behavioural therapy, including exposure and response prevention, is an established treatment for OCD.The next time you find yourself checking the same switch or door lock again, consider whether you have genuinely forgotten the action or are struggling to trust that you remember it correctly. Sometimes, the difficulty is not remembering what you did. It is feeling certain enough to move on.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Meet Mary Engle Pennington, denied a university degree because she was a woman, who went on to transform America’s food safety standards and revolutionise the refrigeration of milk, eggs and meat.
articles.summary: Mary Engle Pennington faced barriers to studying science simply because she was a woman, but went on to become one of America's leading food safety
articles.body: Mary Engle Pennington faced barriers to studying science simply because she was a woman, but went on to become one of America's leading food safety pioneers. After her request to study chemistry was rejected by her school's headmistress, she pursued higher education at the University of Pennsylvania, where women were not awarded degrees at the time. She eventually earned a doctorate in chemistry in 1895 and became the first woman to head the Food Research Laboratory in 1906. Her research transformed the preservation, refrigeration, storage and transportation of perishable foods, helping establish food safety standards across the United States.How did Mary Engle Pennington break barriers in science educationPennington's interest in science developed when she was just 12 years old. After borrowing a copy of Rand's Medical Chemistry from her local library, she became fascinated by the subject. She subsequently asked the headmistress of the private girls' school she attended to introduce a chemistry course. However, her request was rejected because the headmistress believed chemistry was not a subject for girls or women.According to the National Inventors Hall of Fame, Pennington continued pursuing her scientific interests despite the restrictions placed on women's education at the time. When she turned 18, she enrolled at the University of Pennsylvania, where she studied chemistry and biology. In 1892, she received a certificate of proficiency in the subjects because the university did not award degrees to women at the time. Her academic performance, however, was sufficiently impressive for the university to admit her to a graduate programme. She earned her doctorate in chemistry in 1895.How did Mary Engle Pennington improve food safety through refrigerationAfter completing her doctorate, Pennington faced difficulties finding employment. According to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), she established the Philadelphia Clinical Laboratory, where she began conducting bacteriological analyses. One of her early areas of work involved improving the safety of ice cream sold to schoolchildren. She worked to educate farmers about the proper handling of raw milk to help improve the quality of the milk supply.In 1905, Pennington joined the US Department of Agriculture's Bureau of Chemistry. The FDA's historical account states that Harvey Wiley, who headed the Bureau of Chemistry, began working with her on cold-storage problems that year. Her research focused on understanding how refrigeration could help preserve food and prevent bacterial growth. This work became particularly important following the passage of the Pure Food and Drugs Act of 1906, which established a framework for federal regulation of food and drugs.How did Engle Pennington overcome gender discrimination at the FDAIn 1906, Pennington was allowed to apply for the position of chief of the Bureau of Chemistry's Food Research Laboratory. She was initially hesitant because she understood that being a woman could affect her chances of securing the position. However, Wiley encouraged her to take the civil service examination and submitted the hiring request using the name "M.E. Pennington" to conceal her gender.Pennington achieved the highest possible score in the examination and was offered the position. She became the first woman to serve as the FDA's laboratory chief in 1906. The FDA's historical account also describes how Wiley defended her appointment after her gender became known, arguing that civil service law did not permit her exclusion simply because she was a woman.How did Pennington transform food preservation in AmericaFollowing the passage of the 1906 Pure Food and Drugs Act, Pennington's laboratory worked on research that improved the handling and preservation of perishable foods. Her work helped demonstrate that fresh foods could remain usable for longer when maintained at consistently low temperatures. Eliminating temperature fluctuations helped keep bacterial counts low in refrigerated foods, including eggs, milk and cheese.As chief of the Food Research Laboratory, Pennington also developed standards for the safe processing of chicken and procedures to reduce bacterial contamination in milk. She researched methods of storing and transporting poultry, eggs and other perishable products without spoilage. The National Inventors Hall of Fame records that her methods were subsequently adopted across the food-handling industry.How did Pennington transform refrigerated railway transportWhen the United States entered World War I in 1917, Pennington was assigned to the War Food Administration (WFA), an agency associated with future President Herbert Hoover. Its work focused on maximising food production and conservation during the war.One of her responsibilities involved testing the storage and cooling systems of the country's 40,000 refrigerated railway cars. She experimented with different loading racks, ice bunkers and circulation systems to improve the distribution of cold air throughout the carriages. Her research helped establish national standards for ice-cooled refrigerator cars, including standards for their construction and insulation. She also worked on addressing humidity-control problems in cold storage.Pennington emphasised the importance of conserving food during wartime. In a 1917 letter to the St. Louis Railway Club, she wrote: "We are at war…we need food…and that food must be saved." Her work on refrigerated transport contributed to efforts to improve the storage and movement of food supplies across the country.How did Pennington's inventions transform food preservationPennington's work also resulted in several patented inventions. According to the National Inventors Hall of Fame, these included a poultry-cooling rack, a bacteria-resistant method of treating eggs and a sterile container for food products. Her research covered different stages of food preservation, from processing immediately after harvesting or catching to storage and transportation.She also developed an efficient process for scaling, skinning, quick-freezing and dry-packing fish fillets immediately after they were caught. Later in her career, she oversaw the design and construction of both commercial and domestic refrigerators. These projects extended her work beyond government research into the development of refrigeration equipment for wider use.What awards and honours did Mary Engle Pennington receiveIn 1919, Pennington left government service to continue working on food preservation. According to the FDA, she subsequently developed an interest in the safety of frozen foods, which became a major focus in the later years of her professional career.Her contributions received recognition from scientific and professional organisations. In 1940, she received the Garvan Medal from the American Chemical Society. In 1947, she was elected a fellow of the American Society of Refrigeration Engineers, where she served on committees and contributed to the organisation's publications. She was also recognised as an authority on the handling, transportation and storage of perishable foods.Pennington died on December 27, 1952, aged 80. In 1959, she became the first woman inducted into the American Poultry Historical Society Hall of Fame. Much later, in 2018, she was inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame for her contributions to food preservation and storage. Her work on refrigeration, food safety and the transportation of perishable products helped shape practices used throughout the American food supply system.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Licence to kill' row: Child rights and inflation may fuel fresh protests across France
articles.summary: France's streets are once again becoming a battleground over police powers, children's safety and economic hardship.
articles.body: France's streets are once again becoming a battleground over police powers, children's safety and economic hardship.Thousands of demonstrators are expected to take part in fresh rallies on Saturday, marking the fifth consecutive weekend of protests as anger over inflation, alleged police brutality and a controversial firearms bill brings students, trade unions and activists together.The main rally is scheduled to begin in Paris at 1 pm local time, with dozens of other gatherings planned across the country.The Yellow Vest movement is joining high-school students, trade unions and activists campaigning for children's rights and opposing a proposed law that would give police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, AFP reported."Society's in bad shape. We can't focus on one cause more than another," said Claire Bourdille, a member of a collective campaigning against violence targeting children and teenagers.Activists have in recent months demanded stronger safeguards for minors against sexual abuse, making child protection another major focus of the demonstrations.At the centre of Saturday's mobilisation is opposition to a proposed police bill that would grant officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use their firearms.The legislation, which has been approved by France's lower house and is due to go before the Senate, has drawn support from the far-right National Rally, whose leaders argue that police officers should not automatically face suspicion of using disproportionate force.Opponents, however, warn that the proposed law could make it even harder to hold security forces accountable for alleged abuses.Activists have denounced it as a "licence to kill", arguing that it could weaken scrutiny of police shootings in a country where many allegations of police brutality rarely reach criminal courts.Despite the decline in weekend turnout, trade unions have demonstrated that the movement can still draw large crowds. More than 500,000 people took to the streets across France during a union-led strike last Thursday, according to official figures.Unions have now called for another nationwide strike on Tuesday after rejecting the government's proposed 0.6 per cent increase in the minimum wage, dismissing the offer as "crumbs".The protests are unfolding against the backdrop of France's 2027 presidential election, with the far right viewing the vote as its strongest opportunity yet to capture power, AFP reported earlier.Marine Le Pen's National Rally has backed the proposed police bill, bringing the debate over law enforcement, civil liberties and public order into an increasingly charged political climate ahead of the election."You use AI every day. articles.title: Watch: Passengers jump into water as luxury ship collides with tanker on Mississippi River
articles.summary: A video emerged showing the American Heritage river cruise ship sinking into the Mississippi River in New Orleans after colliding with the Atlantic
articles.body: A video emerged showing the American Heritage river cruise ship sinking into the Mississippi River in New Orleans after colliding with the Atlantic Asphalt tanker on Friday. Passengers can be seen panicking and jumping into the water as the five-storey vessel begins to tilt and eventually goes down.Rescue teams, including tugboat operators, dock workers and police personnel, rushed to the scene to pull people from the river.All passengers and crew aboard the cruise ship were rescued, with no one reported missing. At least 32 people were taken to hospital, but none suffered critical injuries, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said. Around 180 people, including passengers and crew, were aboard the vessel when the tanker struck it at the Port of New Orleans.The American Heritage began taking on water and listing sharply within minutes of the collision, triggering a large-scale rescue operation. Dozens of people were pulled from the water, including at least two police officers.The tanker apparently lost steering before crashing into the docked cruise ship."We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi,” Moreno said at a news conference, as rescuers and others cheered.“It was docked right at the Port of New Orleans when a tanker ship lost control and collided into the cruise ship,” Moreno said.The American Heritage began listing within minutes of the collision and eventually flipped while emergency personnel were still working to evacuate those aboard.Dozens of passengers and at least two police officers were pulled from the Mississippi River, where the water temperature was around 19 degrees Celsius.Devon Flanagan, who was working nearby at the Port of New Orleans, said he saw workers rushing towards the dock before noticing that the cruise ship had overturned and passengers were struggling in the water.“It was just chaos,” he said. “You had all types of ships, like other barges and other companies down there trying to help out, which also was a little convoluted because you had people still in the water.”The exact cause of the collision remains unclear. Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said the tanker appeared to have experienced “some type of loss of steering”.The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) was expected to investigate the incident. However, its investigators were initially unable to reach New Orleans after flights across the country were grounded due to communication problems at regional air traffic control centres.Passengers who were not injured were taken to a nearby auditorium, where cruise officials conducted a roll call to ensure everyone was accounted for, Moreno said.Many passengers lost their identification documents and car keys during the incident. Most were visitors from outside New Orleans and needed assistance with accommodation, transportation and other basic arrangements.“They needed chargers for their phones. Some people didn't have phones,” Moreno said. “This has now made national news. They need to contact their families to let them know they're OK. Food, hotel rooms, transportation.”The American Heritage, operated by American Cruise Lines, was completing an eight-day voyage covering several destinations along the Mississippi River in Louisiana and Mississippi.Built in 2015, the 160-metre-long vessel can accommodate up to 150 passengers. It was scheduled to end its journey in New Orleans, according to maritime tracking website MarineTraffic.Martin Davies, a maritime law expert at Tulane University, said it was too early to establish the cause of the collision. However, videos of the incident appeared to indicate a possible catastrophic failure of systems aboard the tanker.He described the circumstances as “super bad luck” because the collision occurred as passengers were departing the cruise ship.Davies said the tanker was travelling upriver against the current at a relatively slow speed.“For something like this to happen for an upbound ship indicates that something must have gone really badly wrong,” Davies said.He added that tankers generally have local pilots aboard to guide them through waterways because of their familiarity with the river and the vessel. The tanker had also completed the difficult Algiers Point turn on the Mississippi River before the collision.According to the International Maritime Organisation, the tanker is owned by Nave Shipping SA, a company registered in Monrovia, Liberia. MarineTraffic identifies it as a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation, a major Chinese state-owned conglomerate.The corporation accounted for nearly a quarter of the global commercial shipbuilding market in 2022 and was also the world's largest military shipbuilder at the time, according to a report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.China State Shipbuilding Corporation did not respond to an emailed request for comment on Friday afternoon.During his first term, US President Donald Trump listed the corporation among more than two dozen Chinese-owned companies that he accused of exploiting “United States investors to finance the development and modernisation” of the Chinese military.The executive order did not freeze all economic transactions involving the listed companies but imposed restrictions on the types of transactions they could undertake on US soil.The Atlantic Asphalt specialises in transporting large quantities of asphalt and bitumen, a semi-solid petroleum-based material commonly used in road construction and roofing, according to MarineTraffic.You use AI every day. articles.summary: GURGAON: A couple returning home on Diwali night had a frightening experience after two men allegedly chased their car, repeatedly attempted to block its
articles.body: GURGAON: A couple returning home on Diwali night had a frightening experience after two men allegedly chased their car, repeatedly attempted to block its path and tried to intercept them on Gurgaon’s Southern Peripheral Road (SPR), near Sector 70, around 11.55pm.The incident took place on Darbaripur Road, barely a kilometre from the couple's residential society. Shubham Jain, who moved to the city around seven months ago, shared details of the incident on social media five days later, along with dashcam footage from his car and CCTV footage from his residential society.In his first post on November 13, Jain described how the incident had left his family shaken."Today after much deliberation and 5 days later I have the courage to post this out here. My family is shook I've moved to Gurgaon about 7 months ago and always thought the road rage , mugging ,kidnapping and robbery were incidents seen on Reels ."According to Jain's account, he was returning home with his wife when a car began following their vehicle. Initially, he assumed that the occupants were attempting to overtake him. However, the situation took a frightening turn when the car overtook his vehicle, braked abruptly in front of it and the occupants allegedly attempted to get out."It's finally hit home. On Diwali Night around 11:55 PM in the night I was returning back home with my wife , just 1 km away from home on Darbaripur Road , Sector 70 SPR i was tailed and chased like a full movie scene At first I thought it was just someone trying to overtake," he wrote.Realising that something was wrong, Jain accelerated his car in an attempt to reach the safety of his residential society. He said the other vehicle repeatedly tried to cut across his car and block its path during the chase.The dashcam footage shared by Jain captures the overtaking, abrupt braking and repeated attempts by the other vehicle to obstruct his car. The couple eventually managed to reach their society's entrance, where three security personnel intervened and stopped the other vehicle. A man is seen stepping out of the vehicle and appearing to argue with the guards.Jain said the occupants remained at the society gates for nearly 20 minutes and argued with security guards over being allowed to enter. He also alleged that one of the men threatened the security personnel, saying that if the car was spotted again, it would be taken care of.In his social media post, Jain claimed that the car had no rear number plate and its front registration details had been obscured. He described the two occupants as one man in his mid-20s and another in his late teens.Jain's post also mentioned the name Manoj Kumar and vehicle registration number HR76D0402 in connection with the incident. However, police are yet to establish the identity of the vehicle's registered owner and verify the registration number's connection with the car seen in the footage.The society's security personnel also allegedly told Jain that such incidents were common in the area and that the men were local residents. Only to be saved by private security ? The man has the audacity to fight with them and tell them if the car is spotted again it will be taken care of !!!!!"He also tagged Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini and senior police officials, urging them to take note of the incident.Expressing disappointment over the safety situation in the city, Jain wrote: "This is what a truly global city offers ? I'm truly truly sad about the state of law and order in the state after the Faridabad incident and now this happening first hand."The incident gained attention after Jain's post and accompanying videos circulated on social media. articles.title: Singer's Hall of Fame induction axed over Russell Brand comments
articles.summary: The Liverpool Beatles Museum says the ex-Icicles Works frontman will not be honoured in their Hall of Fame.
articles.body:
Singer Ian McNabb will no longer be inducted into a music Hall of Fame after publicly defending convicted rapist Russell Brand.

The former frontman of Liverpool rock band The Icicle Works claimed Brand had been "stitched up".

Brand, 51, was jailed for 10 years and six months on Monday after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

The Liverpool Beatles Museum had planned to induct McNabb into its Liverpool Legends Hall of Fame, but has now shelved the plans following his comments.

McNabb, 66, posted on social media about the disgraced television comic.

He wrote: "Russell Brand is being stitched up for his outspoken views.

"He got close to the target and he has a big audience.

"I know people who were in his orbit and girls were throwing themselves at him every night.

"If that happened to me I know what I would do."

The post led to the cancellation of all of McNabb's upcoming shows.

Ewan McNaught, of Scottish promotions company Renegade Communions, cancelled planned concerts in Glasgow, Edinburgh and Newcastle.

Writing online, he said: "I hate cancelling gigs, and it's the first time in my career that I've had to do it, but not only can I not defend Ian McNabb's disgraceful social media comments in support of Russell Brand, as a husband and a father of a young daughter, I simply can't work with him moving forward."

McNabb later deleted his post and told followers he had "been cancelled".

He added: "In no way did I mean to cause offence to those who have been abused sexually either recently or in past times, however long ago.

"I have committed no crime to my knowledge, but understand the upset I have caused."

The Icicle Works' biggest UK hit was Love Is a Wonderful Colour, which reached number 15 in 1984.

A spokesperson for the Liverpool Beatles Museum said: "Under the circumstances, Ian McNabb will not be inducted."

articles.title: Serial Ilford fly-tipper tracked down and prosecuted
articles.summary: Carmen Vasile left bin bags and trolleys full of waste in several locations in east London.
articles.body:
A fly-tipper who repeatedly dumped trolleys full of rubbish in Ilford, east London, has been ordered to pay a total of £1,019 in fines and costs and given a community order.

Carmen Vasile, 45, pleaded guilty at Barkingside Magistrates' Court in September to three counts of fly-tipping.

She had previously been given multiple warnings by enforcement officers and a legal notice telling her how to dispose of household waste. After a fixed penalty notice went unpaid, the council took legal action.

Councillor Sunny Brar, Redbridge's cabinet member for enforcement, said: "This prosecution should serve as a warning that we have zero tolerance for fly-tipping in Redbridge."

Among the waste she illegally dumped in Yoxley Approach was a shopping trolley filled with a foldable table, a plastic baby bath, a baby-changing table and bags of rubbish.

She left another trolley full of sealed black bin bags in Bentley Drive.

Several open bin bags, loose household waste and a delivery box scattered across the pavement in Bentley Drive were also traced back to Vasile by Redbridge Council's enforcement team.

Vasile was handed a year's community order, including a seven-day rehabilitation programme.

She also received a five-year criminal behaviour order, putting strict legal controls and conditions on how rubbish is stored and disposed of by anyone living at her Yoxley Drive address.

Brar said Vasile's case was "a great example of what can be done when communities work with us to bring offenders to justice.

"Information from the public and evidence from our enforcement team's investigations helped build a robust case to obtain the strongest sentence possible."

articles.title: In 1944, 19-year-old Marine Henry Keen recorded a July 4 message for his family at a Hollywood USO; killed at Iwo Jima eight months later, it remains his only known recording
articles.summary: Discover the touching story of Marine Henry L. Keen and his last recorded message home from a Hollywood USO in 1944, just eight months before his death at Iwo Jima during World War II.
articles.body: A short recording made at a Hollywood USO in 1944 preserved something a family could never expect to lose: the sound of their son's voice. According to the Mississippi Armed Forces Museum, on July 4, that year, 19-year-old Marine Henry L. Keen recorded a personal message for his mother in Braxton, Mississippi. He spoke about life in Hollywood, asked whether his father had been fishing and told his mother she could expect him home around the fourteenth. The recording remains the only known audio recording of him. The Mississippi Armed Forces Museum preserves the recording and publishes its full transcript, offering a rare glimpse into the everyday thoughts of a young Marine during World War II.A message recorded at the Hollywood USOKeen’s message was part of a wartime project called “Voices of Victory,” produced by GEM Razors and Blades. The project allowed military personnel to record personal messages for relatives waiting at home. According to the Mississippi Armed Forces Museum, these messages were stored on lacquered cardboard discs that families could keep and play. Keen was stationed in California when he visited the Hollywood USO on Independence Day 1944. A woman introduced the recording by addressing his mother, Mrs. Keen, in Braxton, Mississippi. She explained that the message was from the Hollywood USO before handing the recording over to him.Keen began by greeting his family and joking about being in “good old LA” before correcting himself to “Hollywood”. He said he was having a good time and hoped everyone at home was doing well. He also asked about his father, wondering whether he had been fishing. The young Marine mentioned that he was with a couple of friends. He described the USO as a welcoming place with free food, drinks, music, records and an orchestra. His message sounded relaxed, with casual remarks about his surroundings and the people he was spending time with. He told his family that they could expect him home around the fourteenth and imagined himself knocking at the door. Near the end, a woman prompted him to tell his mother that he loved her. Keen initially said goodbye, but after another prompt, he added, “Love y’all. Son.” The original audio recording preserved these small details, including his pauses, jokes and affectionate sign-off.Eight months later, Keen was killed at Iwo JimaIt was not the reunion Keen had envisioned. According to the Mississippi Armed Forces Museum archives, PFC Henry L. Keen was killed in action at Iwo Jima only eight months later from the time when the recording was made. The Battle of Iwo Jima occurred in February-March 1945 and was a part of the Pacific Theatre operations during World War II. It was a bloody battle, one of the costliest battles for the Americans during the war. There is no information provided by the museum about the details of Keen’s death. All that is known is that he died in the Battle of Iwo Jima and left behind his recording of July 1944.As stated in the museum, the July 4 disc is the only recording of Keen that survived. Unlike a picture or military service record, the recording offered more than proof that he existed, because he was speaking directly to his mother. There was nothing extraordinary in the message that lacked any rhetoric about the war and prediction of the future. The disc only held a teen talking about his friends, eating, listening to music, fishing and coming back home.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Canada, US make progress on trade deal as Mark Carney pursues new Asian markets
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announces progress in trade negotiations with the US, while Canada seeks to diversify its market ties with Asia, including significant agreements with ASEAN and the Philippines.
articles.body: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has said negotiations with the United States are moving forward, following a lengthy conversation with President Donald Trump and senior officials, even as Ottawa works to expand trade ties across Asia and reduce its reliance on the American market.Speaking to reporters in Manila on Saturday, Carney said he had a “quite a long, substantive conversation” with Trump shortly before leaving for his trip to Europe and Asia.“We are making progress. There is the possibility of a deal, a bilateral deal. But we’re not yet there,” he said.US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Trump's newly appointed White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, also took part in the discussion, Carney said.Ottawa, however, is not prepared to accept terms that could weaken its automotive industry, which has faced pressure from US tariffs.The latest discussions follow the breakdown of trade negotiations in August, when Canada suspended talks over last-minute demands from Washington that it considered unacceptable. The US subsequently imposed 50% tariffs on around $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, prompting Canada to introduce retaliatory duties in September. Negotiations have since resumed.A potential agreement could ease some of the tariffs affecting major industries, including steel and aluminium. However, the scope of any deal remains uncertain.Before the US midterm elections, Trump said the two countries were close to reaching an agreement. Carney later indicated that Washington had withdrawn demands concerning Canadian cultural policies, French-language protections and Ottawa's ability to negotiate trade agreements with other countries.Trade tensions also became an issue during the midterm campaign. Democrats criticised the tariffs, linking them to higher consumer prices and promising to challenge the measures.Their electoral gains have complicated Canada's negotiating position. Ottawa must now weigh the possibility of securing partial tariff relief through an agreement against holding out for broader free-trade access as Congress prepares to scrutinise the existing measures.While discussions with Washington continue, Carney announced progress on two separate trade arrangements in Southeast Asia.Canada has substantially concluded negotiations on a free-trade agreement with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), a regional bloc representing nearly 700 million people. Ottawa has also completed negotiations on a separate agreement with the Philippines.The Canadian government estimates that the ASEAN deal could add nearly 2 billion Canadian dollars (US$1.4 billion) to the country's economy and support close to 14,000 jobs, particularly across agriculture and manufacturing. Officials expect to sign the agreement next year.The proposed Philippines agreement would cover more than 90% of tariff lines, Carney said. Ottawa expects the arrangement to help triple Canadian exports to the country by 2035, with formal signing also anticipated next year.Both agreements form part of Canada's wider strategy to diversify its export markets amid uncertainty over its trade relationship with the US.Carney has set a target of doubling Canadian exports to markets outside the US by 2035, making trade diversification a central part of his government's economic agenda.His visit to Manila comes ahead of a three-day ASEAN summit involving regional leaders and representatives from partner countries, beginning on Sunday.The prime minister previously attended the European Political Community summit in Ireland. His itinerary also includes the Francophonie summit in Cambodia and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, where he is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russian couple behind Empire State Building climb could face deportation after plea deal falls through
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Russian couple who went viral after scaling the Empire State Building in New York and unfurling a banner carrying a message of love and peace
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Russian couple who went viral after scaling the Empire State Building in New York and unfurling a banner carrying a message of love and peace before an apparent marriage proposal could face deportation from the US after a plea deal with prosecutors fell through.Angela Nikolau, 33, and Ivan Kuznetsov, 32, appeared in a New York criminal court on Thursday (November 12), where their lawyer said an agreement to plead guilty to misdemeanour charges had been withdrawn. Nikolau was seen tearing up during the hearing as the possibility of deportation emerged.The couple had reportedly been negotiating a deal with prosecutors that would have allowed them to avoid what their lawyer described as serious immigration consequences. However, according to Fox News, the Manhattan District Attorney's Office withdrew the offer through an email sent the night before the hearing."We didn't damage any property. We didn't intend to put anyone in danger. We just wanted to send a message of love, and we're ready to defend ourselves," Kuznetsov told reporters."We wanted to share a message of peace. With so much pain in the world today, we wanted to create a performance to stay in the people's hearts," Nikolau added.Lawyer warns of consequences if couple is deported to RussiaNoam Biale, the couple's attorney, said his team had accepted an offer from prosecutors for the pair to plead guilty to misdemeanour charges in exchange for protection from what he called "catastrophic immigration consequences".The deal, however, was taken off the table shortly before the hearing."If sent back to Russia, Mr Kuznetsov will almost certainly be sent to fight in the war in Ukraine and Ms Nikolau may be jailed for her artistic expression," Biale said.The couple, originally from Moscow, were charged with felony reckless endangerment, burglary and other offences following their climb in July. Their lawyer's latest comments have raised concerns over the potential immigration consequences of the criminal proceedings.Couple climbed 1,454 feet to unfurl banner and proposeThe incident took place on July 2, when Nikolau and Kuznetsov climbed the Empire State Building's broadcast antenna, reaching a height of around 1,454 feet (443 metres) above Manhattan.After reaching the top, they unfurled a black banner carrying the message: "When the power of love beats the love of power the world knows peace".Kuznetsov then proposed to Nikolau on a ledge slightly below the antenna's peak. The couple later shared pictures of the stunt on social media.According to the criminal complaint, police found a broken lock on a security door on the building's restricted-access 104th floor, which provides access to the antenna. The highest floor open to visitors is the 102nd-floor observation deck.Police waited for around half an hour for the antenna to be powered down before officers from the Emergency Services Unit began climbing the structure. They eventually intercepted the couple as they were making their way down.Authorities said the unauthorised climb also put responding officers at risk, with personnel required to ascend to around 1,250 feet (381 metres).The Empire State Building's management described the climb as unauthorised.Couple featured in Netflix documentaryNikolau and Kuznetsov, who also goes by the name Ivan Beerkus, are known for climbing skyscrapers and other tall structures, often without authorisation.Their relationship and rooftop-climbing exploits were featured in the 2024 Netflix documentary Skywalkers: A Love Story. The film followed the couple as they undertook dangerous climbs of tall buildings and explored their relationship.The documentary premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2024.You use AI every day.
