articles.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
articles.summary: The Ukrainian president says US envoys touted the exchange as part of efforts to end the war with Russia.
articles.body:
US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

The Ukrainian president's comments on Saturday come after US envoys visited Moscow and an EU summit in Dublin as part of ongoing efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.

Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance to deter future threats, but this previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border was unacceptable.

Zelensky has also consistently said Ukraine was unwilling to give up sovereign territory, despite Moscow's demands for it to cede the Donbas.

"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky told reporters on Saturday.

He went on to say that if he received a proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum.

US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow's demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider.

Moscow has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal.

Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion.

There have, however, been recent signs the two can find common ground: last month, US First Lady Melania Trump was able to broker a temporary ceasefire in the the Kherson region to allow for evacuations and aid deliveries.

US officials had previously said that Ukrainian Nato membership was off the table.

Zelensky said on Saturday that the US proposal made him believe that "Nato is back on the agenda".

But he cautioned: "You have also heard Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."

Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas.

Ceding the small portions of land Ukraine still controls there would be symbolically significant for Kyiv because it would constitute an acceptance of the Donbas being Russian.

Zelensky has previously spoken of retaking Russian-controlled territory in four of Ukraine's regions, as well as the Crimean peninsula, which Moscow annexed in 2014.

The latest round of talks come after a period of fraught relations between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia, which US President Donald Trump had asked Ukraine to pause to facilitate the supply of Russian diesel to ease global fuel prices, which have been rising since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February.

Zelensky then accused US officials of limiting Ukraine's Starlink internet service , which it uses to co-ordinate defensive operations, while Trump said it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president" and called for fresh elections.

Elections are suspended while Ukraine remains under martial law, but Zelensky has previously said he was willing to hold them within months of a peace deal being reached and would give up the presidency in exchange for Nato membership.

articles.title: Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister
articles.summary: Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised a sweeping anti-corruption drive after ousting Orbán in April.
articles.body:
Nearly $20m (£14.8m) in cash has been found hidden in farm buildings and buried in forests as part of an investigation into a former minister of Viktor Orbán, authorities have said.

Miklós Seszták, who served as minister of national development for four of the ex-prime minister's 16-year rule, is accused of accepting bribes as part of a scheme involving the state transport company. He has denied any wrongdoing.

Hungary's new Prime Minister Péter Magyar unseated Orbán in a landslide election in April on the promise of launching a sweeping anti-corruption drive.

On Friday, following the two-day search for the cash - found in secluded locations across the country - Magyar described it as the end of the "mafia".

Investigators found wads of banknotes in safes, buried in woodlands and hidden in agricultural and residential buildings and warehouses, as part of the probe into Seszták, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) said in a statement.

The cash amounted to "5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and $1,257,100", it added, bringing the combined value to $19.5m. It has been deposited into the Hungarian State Treasury, the body said.

The NVVH was established to investigate allegations of corruption during the Orbán rule, which Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory".

Magyar promised Hungarians "regime change" during the election earlier this year and has set about undoing many Orbán-era policies since entering office.

Allegations of corruption and cronyism have long dogged Orbán, who during the course of his tenure turned Hungary into what the EU characterised as an "electoral autocracy".

His government faced accusations of offering lucrative government projects to allies. Orbán has strongly denied the claims.

Two of his former ministers, including Seszták, and the former central bank chief Gyorgy Matolcsy have been under arrest since September over accusations of graft in separate investigations. They all deny wrongdoing.

On Monday, Hungarian authorities also detained Orbán's brother and three others as part of a people-smuggling case.

The former prime minister ​dismissed it as political revenge, saying: "In this dirty game, ​the aim is the elimination of the political opponent and the establishment of a one-party system.

"I am the target, my younger brother is just a tool."

articles.body: PATNA: A land dispute involving BJP MLA and renowned folk singer Maithili Thakur has intensified in Darbhanga, even after a nearly 100-metre stretch of a disputed road was demolished late on Friday night.Amid mounting opposition from villagers, Thakur and her father, Ramesh Thakur, allegedly deployed a bulldozer to remove the brick-laid pathway and a wall constructed along it. However, the demolition has done little to ease tensions in Pokharbhinda panchayat of Tardih block.Villagers allege that portions of their private land remain encroached upon and enclosed by boundary walls. They maintain that removing the disputed road alone will not resolve the matter unless the alleged occupation of their plots is also addressed.The controversy has drawn a political response from RJD leader Vinod Mishra, who contested the Assembly election against Maithili Thakur. Mishra has highlighted allegations involving the land of several villagers and urged the MLA to intervene and resolve the matter in a manner that respects local sentiments.According to Mishra, allegations of encroachment have been raised over 12 dhurs of land belonging to Gagan Mishra, 27 dhurs belonging to Chandra Mohan Mishra and one kattha belonging to Ram Udgar Mishra. He also claimed that excavation near Shrawan Kumar Mishra's plot had damaged the land.Mishra said Maithili Thakur had earned considerable respect among people as a folk singer and should take the villagers' concerns seriously. He urged her to ensure that those whose land had allegedly been occupied were given back their property.The villagers, meanwhile, have expressed disappointment, saying they had voted for Thakur and sent her to the Assembly but were now facing a land dispute involving her family. They have accused her father of allegedly occupying government land, a public pathway, a common cremation and last-rites site, and private plots.Their complaints also concern construction near the common last-rites site close to Tiwari Baba Sthan and the alleged obstruction of the public road connecting Shashinath Mishra Chowk to the Waterways. Residents say farmers use the route to reach their fields and that construction along it has affected movement.Other allegations include encroachment on 14 dhurs of a three-kattha plot belonging to Bhagwan Mishra and a separate claim by Ramudar Mishra over 15 dhurs of land. Villagers have also complained that a drain flowing out of a pond was filled with soil and that part of the land belonging to the drain was allegedly used for road construction.Concerns have also been raised over soil excavation near ancestral memorials and private plots. Ramday Devi has apprehended damage to her land, while villagers fear that the excavation could also pose a risk to a nearby government transformer.Residents have submitted complaints to the administration, the Chief Minister's Office and the state government's Sahyog portal, seeking an impartial inquiry and the removal of alleged encroachments.Taking cognisance of the complaints, in-charge Circle Officer Alok Kumar has ordered an inquiry. Both sides will be called to a public hearing to present their claims, following which land documents will be examined and further action taken.For now, the demolition of the 100-metre stretch marks a significant development. articles.title: Russian billionaire’s $600 million high-tech superyacht, dubbed ugliest in the world, is ‘stuck’ in Italy; it takes $11 million a year to keep its systems running
articles.summary: Italian authorities have reportedly been stuck with an unusual and expensive responsibility for more than four years: paying to keep a Russian
articles.body: Italian authorities have reportedly been stuck with an unusual and expensive responsibility for more than four years: paying to keep a Russian billionaire’s $600 million superyacht in pristine condition. Sailing Yacht A, owned by Russian industrialist Andrey Melnichenko who has brought in new technologies in his businesses, has been sitting in the port of Trieste since March 2022, when Italian authorities seized it under international sanctions. Even though the futuristic vessel cannot leave the dock, it still requires constant maintenance, a working crew and nonstop power.Even worse for Italy’s budget, authorities cannot simply shut the ship down to save money. Inside the yacht sits a multimillion-euro private art collection, including paintings by Claude Monet, that would deteriorate if the air conditioning were turned off.Super-yacht needs $30,000 per day just to sit in portAccording to the French newspaper Le Parisien, keeping Sailing Yacht A, reportedly dubbed the world’s ugliest superyacht, in working order costs roughly $30,000 a day, or nearly $11 million a year. That money pays for a 20-person skeleton crew tasked with cleaning the vessel and running its onboard systems, along with specialized upkeep, insurance, climate control and fuel.Sailing Yacht A is powered by four variable-speed generators, each capable of producing 2,800 kW, for a combined capacity of 11.2 megawatts. Depending on the ship's power needs at any given moment, those generators burn through roughly 400 gallons of diesel every hour to run essential machinery and protect the interiors from decay.The financial headache could soon get much worse. A report published in July noted that Italy may have to spend another $12 million on the yacht as it nears a mandatory class-renewal survey. While the initial certification costs far less, the technical repairs required to pass inspection could run into the millions – a bill the Italian Treasury might have to advance.Why Italy can’t switch off the air conditioningThe strangest part of the maintenance bill is hidden inside the ship. In January 2023, an investigation by the Italian television program Le Iene revealed that Sailing Yacht A holds at least eight paintings, including works by Claude Monet and other Impressionists, as well as pieces by 17th- and 18th-century French artists.A regional fine-arts official who inspected the collection explained that the paintings require stable temperatures to survive. As canvas, wooden supports and layers of paint react differently to moisture, swinging temperatures and humidity can cause surfaces to warp, crack and flake. Too much humidity also invites mold and condensation behind the frames.As a result, the yacht’s climate-control systems are a preservation necessity. Switching off the power to save on diesel could trigger far more expensive damage to the artwork.The yacht features three massive masts, eight decks, multiple elevators and suspended spiral staircases. Its interiors are outfitted with dark wood, copper accents, patterned carpets, integrated bookcases, and a multilevel main salon.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? articles.title: A Tennessee couple moved their household belongings into two storage units after selling their home, then found both nearly emptied; judges upheld $33,500 in damages and $23,700 in fees over fake security claims
articles.summary: A storage facility is supposed to provide a safe place for belongings that cannot immediately be moved into a new home.
articles.body: A storage facility is supposed to provide a safe place for belongings that cannot immediately be moved into a new home. But a Tennessee couple who rented two units after selling their house discovered that almost everything they had stored was missing, despite being assured that the facility had security cameras and regular patrols. Their investigation raised further questions about the locks, the facility owner's security claims and the handling of earlier theft complaints.In a November 6, 2026, decision available on Justia, the Tennessee Court of Appeals upheld a judgment against Posey Storage Solutions and its owner, Tim Posey, in a lawsuit brought by Nathan and Devan Dickey. The court affirmed $33,500 in damages and a separate award of $23,700 in attorney's fees and expenses. It found that the trial court had sufficient evidence to hold the owner liable for fraudulent misrepresentation, gross negligence, theft-related claims and violations of the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act.How the couple's belongings disappearedThe dispute began in December 2019, when Devan Dickey contacted Posey about renting storage space. The couple were selling their home and preparing to move away from the area, so they needed two units to keep their household belongings.According to Devan's testimony, Posey described the facility's security arrangements, pointing out cameras installed around the buildings and saying that he regularly patrolled the premises three to four times a day. He also recommended two locks sold by the facility, describing them as stronger than commercially available alternatives and difficult to cut with bolt cutters. The couple purchased the locks for $10 each. However, Posey did not disclose that he retained a master key that could open them.The two units contained valuable household and work-related belongings. One held furniture, a mattress and sentimental items inherited by Devan from her grandmother. The other contained Nathan's expensive work equipment, valued at approximately $28,350. In November 2020, Nathan returned to the facility to retrieve a welding hood and discovered that almost everything in his unit had disappeared. Only a table and a crockpot remained. He contacted the police and checked his wife's unit, which initially appeared untouched.Several weeks later, the couple returned to collect the remaining belongings and discovered that Devan's unit had also been almost completely emptied. Its lock appeared intact, and only damaged Christmas ornaments and a broken blanket ladder remained.Why the security claims became importantWhen the couple first reported the thefts, Posey told them he would review the surveillance footage. He also suggested that he suspected one of his workers might have been responsible. However, no footage was ever provided. Posey later failed to attend a scheduled meeting with the couple and stopped responding to their calls. The Dickeys subsequently discovered that the cameras were not functional. They also learned that Posey retained master keys to the locks he sold customers.Evidence presented during the trial revealed earlier theft complaints involving the facility. Two former customers, Ann Harrod and Cynthia Sarapata, testified about missing belongings and their unsuccessful attempts to obtain assistance from Posey. Police records also documented multiple theft and burglary reports involving the property between 2015 and 2021.The trial court found that Posey had misrepresented the facility's security arrangements to persuade the Dickeys to rent the units. It also concluded that he had failed to properly supervise an individual who had access to the master keys.Why the storage owner was held liableThe trial court found Posey liable for fraudulent misrepresentation, negligence, gross negligence, negligent supervision, theft-related conversion and violations of the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act (TCPA). It concluded that the owner knew the cameras were fake but continued presenting them as working security equipment. It also found that he had failed to disclose the master keys and allowed an employee access without adequate supervision.Posey argued that the rental agreement protected him from liability because it stated that the facility would not be responsible for property lost through theft or other causes. However, the appeals court agreed with the trial court that he had failed to properly raise this contractual defence in his legal response.The court also explained that such an exclusion could not protect a business from liability for gross negligence, reckless conduct or intentional wrongdoing. Under Tennessee law, consumer protection rights under the TCPA cannot simply be waived through a contract. The appeals court further rejected the argument that statements made outside the written rental agreement should have been excluded. Evidence of those statements was relevant to the fraud and consumer protection claims.What the appeals court decidedThe Tennessee Court of Appeals gave considerable weight to the trial court's assessment of Posey's credibility. It noted that his testimony had changed between his deposition and the trial, and that he had been contradicted by evidence concerning previous theft complaints and the facility's security arrangements.The trial court had concluded that the overwhelming evidence indicated Posey was responsible for the burglaries himself or had authorised or failed to supervise an employee who committed the thefts. The appeals court found sufficient evidence supporting the judgment and declined to disturb those findings. The owner also failed to properly challenge the merits of several findings, including the fraudulent misrepresentation and consumer protection claims.In its November 6, 2026, decision, the appeals court affirmed the trial court's judgment in its entirety and remanded the case. The $33,500 damages award and $23,700 in attorney's fees and expenses therefore remained in place. The court also assessed the costs of the appeal against Posey and Posey Storage Solutions. Overall, the ruling highlights that storage businesses cannot rely on broad contractual disclaimers to escape responsibility for deceptive security claims or grossly negligent conduct. It also reinforces the importance of truthful representations when businesses promise customers that their belongings will be protected.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Natalee Holloway's confessed killer caught trying to extort $250K from grieving mother in FBI sting video
articles.summary: Previously unseen FBI sting video captures Joran van der Sloot's attempt to extort Beth Holloway for information about her daughter Natalee Holloway.
articles.body: Joran van der Sloot spent years tormenting Natalee Holloway's family with a tangled web of lies. But behind closed doors, the convicted killer was playing an even more sinister game. Now, previously unseen video from an FBI sting reveals just how far he was willing to go to exploit a grieving mother's desperate search for answers. The Netflix true crime docuseries "Taken: Natalee Holloway," co-directed by Dani Sloane and Matthew Galkin, features video of the 2010 sting operation showing the Dutch national attempting to extort money from Holloway's family. "His brazenness stood out to me, the fact that he's sitting across from lawyer John Q. Kelly, and he's going 'Can I have a soda? It's so hot outside, I had to wait for a cab,'" Sloane told Fox News Digital. "He's having a casual conversation while he's extorting the mother of his victim for money, for information that only he knows. It's astonishing. You really don't often get to look at a perpetrator like that. He feels really cavalier and he's just casual about the whole thing." SERIAL KILLER SURVIVOR WHO ESCAPED 18-HOUR CAPTIVITY REVEALS INSTINCT SHE WISHES SHE NEVER IGNORED "It’s pretty haunting to see," Sloane added. Holloway, 18, disappeared on May 30, 2005, while she was on a graduation trip in Aruba with her high school classmates. She was last seen leaving a bar with van der Sloot, a student at an international school on the Caribbean island where he grew up. Van der Sloot, long suspected in connection with her disappearance, was never charged with her murder. A judge declared Holloway dead in 2012, but her body was never found. Nearly five years after Holloway's disappearance, van der Sloot emailed Kelly, an attorney for Holloway's mother, Beth Holloway, the film revealed. For $250,000, he offered to provide information about Holloway's death and the whereabouts of her remains. Kelly and van der Sloot agreed to meet at a hotel in Aruba in May 2010, where Kelly would hand over a $25,000 deposit in exchange for the information, starting with $10,000 in cash. By then, according to the documentary, van der Sloot had changed his story about what happened to the Alabama teen roughly 40 times. "Joran went on TV countless times and continued to tell slightly different fabricated stories," Sloane said. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X "I think it's probably an even higher number than that. We did our own approximations and it's a pretty staggering number of different stories he told, even just small details he changed within the storytelling about what happened that night. It's astonishing. I've been doing this for a really long time, but I personally have never seen anything like this where it's very clear who did this." "He is so masterful at evading law enforcement and evading consequences by just outright lying," Sloane added. According to the film, Beth agreed to give van der Sloot $25,000 because she believed it was her chance to finally learn what happened to her daughter from the man she had long suspected of killing her. She was on standby at an Alabama bank, ready to wire the remaining $15,000 as soon as van der Sloot signed their agreement. Beth subsequently wired the remaining $15,000 to van der Sloot's bank account, bringing the initial payment to $25,000. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL Before the meeting, Kelly had contacted the FBI, which worked with police in Aruba to secretly record the exchange in hopes of building a criminal case against van der Sloot. The previously unreleased video of the exchange shows Kelly handing over $10,000. "To be completely honest, for me, the biggest deal is the 225 afterwards," van der Sloot tells Kelly in the recording. "Did you put in the contract that that would be paid within a month?" SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS Kelly said yes and van der Sloot signed the agreement. In the docuseries, Kelly explained that van der Sloot was never going to receive the remaining $225,000. "If he disclosed Natalee's whereabouts then he was going to be arrested for it," Kelly explained. "And if he didn't disclose what happened to Natalee, he was going to get arrested anyway for extortion or fraud." Van der Sloot then took Kelly to a nearby house, claiming Holloway's body had been buried in the foundation while the home was under construction. SEND US A TIP "It's honestly a horrific thing to watch," Sloane said. "Just to see how that conversation played out is really stunning." Investigators determined the information was false. But before U.S. authorities could file charges against van der Sloot, he left Aruba for Peru. SIGN UP TO GET THE TRUE CRIME NEWSLETTER Van der Sloot's trail of lies was about to take an even deadlier turn. On May 30, 2010, exactly five years after Holloway's disappearance, van der Sloot murdered 21-year-old Stephany Flores Ramírez in his hotel room in Lima, Peru. According to the film, van der Sloot told investigators he attacked Flores Ramírez after she discovered information about Holloway's disappearance on his laptop. He beat and strangled her. In July 2014, van der Sloot married Leidy Figueroa, a Peruvian woman. They later had a daughter. In the film, retired FBI special agent Alexandra Montilla recalled an encounter in which the "charismatic" van der Sloot told her about a pet rabbit he shared with his daughter. According to Montilla's account, the rabbit scratched his daughter while she was petting it. Montilla said van der Sloot told her that he grabbed the animal and "ripped his head off." LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "I've dealt with a lot of criminals and, as a female, I thought this is probably one of the most dangerous ones," Montilla said. Sloane said Montilla still vividly remembers the encounter. GET REAL-TIME UPDATES DIRECTLY ON THE TRUE CRIME HUB "It really lives in her memory," Sloane said. "It's something that stands out to her out of all the offenders and perpetrators she has spent time with. It counts a lot when a seasoned member of the FBI is horrified by something." In June 2023, van der Sloot was temporarily transferred from Peru to the United States to face federal extortion and wire fraud charges stemming from his 2010 scheme targeting Beth. On Oct. 18, 2023, he pleaded guilty to both charges in federal court in Alabama and was sentenced to 20 years in prison, to be served concurrently with his Peruvian prison sentence. If van der Sloot is released from prison in Peru before completing his U.S. sentence, he would serve the remaining time in the United States. As part of his plea agreement, van der Sloot also confessed to killing Holloway in 2005. The convicted killer said he struck her in the head with a cinder block after she rejected his sexual advances, then disposed of her body in the ocean. This time, Beth said she believed he was telling the truth. "This case was difficult to solve," Sloane said. "There were no forensics to speak of. Natalee’s remains were never found and have never been found to this day. All of this hinged on dealing with Joran. It was incredibly difficult for anyone that was interrogating him to pin him down. He was good at spinning a story. This was someone who told years of stories, one more outlandish than the next about what happened to Natalee." Beth spent nearly two decades seeking answers about her daughter's disappearance and now advocates for other families of missing people. Sloane said that while Beth finally has answers about Holloway's death, she continues to live with the loss of her daughter every day. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE "I think Natalee would be proud of all of us," Beth says in the film. "I think Joran tangled with the wrong girl."

articles.title: Crumpsall murder investigation after man's 'shocking' stabbing
articles.summary: Police say a 27-year-old man died after being stabbed in the "shocking and tragic attack" in Crumpsall.
articles.body:
A murder investigation has been launched after a 27-year-old man was stabbed in Manchester.

Officers were called to Moss Bank in the Crumpsall area of the city shortly after 01:30 GMT following reports that a man had suffered several stab wounds. He later died from his injuries in an ambulance.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said initial inquiries suggested the victim had been attacked by "a number of males" all believed to have been wearing dark clothing and balaclavas.

The suspects are believed to have fled the scene in the direction of Ash Tree Road, said a force spokesperson who added that no arrests had been made and inquiries were continuing.

Forensics officers could be seen lifting drain covers within the area and looking under cars parked along the street lined with terraced houses.

One officer climbed a fence near an alley.

A police spokesperson said the victim's family had been informed and were being supported by specially trained officers.

"First and foremost, my thoughts are with the victim's family and loved ones at this devastating time," said Det Insp Neil Higginson.

"This was a shocking and tragic attack which has resulted in a young man losing his life.

"I would like to reassure the community that we are pursuing all available lines of inquiry.

"I would urge anyone who witnessed the incident or has any information that could assist our investigation to contact us."

articles.title: Why did a Brooklyn building collapse suddenly, killing eight? Experts point to excavation work at neighbouring construction site
articles.summary: The sudden collapse of a three-storey building in Brooklyn, New York, that killed at least eight people has raised questions about construction safety and
articles.body: The sudden collapse of a three-storey building in Brooklyn, New York, that killed at least eight people has raised questions about construction safety and whether excavation work at an adjoining site destabilised the structure. The building, located in the Flatbush neighbourhood, collapsed on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, plunging into an excavation pit at an adjacent construction site. At least 17 people were injured. The disaster triggered a major rescue operation involving around 250 firefighters and emergency responders.Structural engineers believe inadequate support for the soil surrounding the construction site could have played a crucial role in the collapse.According to experts interviewed by Scientific American, excavation work close to an existing building can destabilize its foundations if the surrounding soil is not adequately supported.Michael Chajes, a professor of civil and environmental engineering at the University of Delaware, said vibrations from construction machinery could have weakened the soil supporting the neighbouring structure. He suggested that the vibrations may have undermined the building, redistributed the forces acting on it and eventually triggered its collapse.How can excavation cause a building to collapse?When construction workers excavate land next to an existing building, they must install temporary support systems, commonly known as shoring, to prevent the surrounding soil from shifting or collapsing. These systems can include steel piles driven into the ground, with boards or other materials placed between them to hold the soil in position.Gregory Deierlein, a civil and environmental engineer at Stanford University, explained that supporting the soil becomes particularly challenging when excavation takes place immediately next to an existing building. The soil is already under pressure from the neighbouring structure. If the temporary support system is not sufficiently strong or rigid, the ground can shift, potentially destabilising the building's foundation. The design must account for several factors, including the type of soil, the weight of the neighbouring building and the depth of its foundation. Heavy construction machinery can also generate vibrations that disturb the soil and affect the stability of temporary supports.Mehrdad Sasani, a civil engineering professor at Northeastern University, said the vibrations from construction equipment could have contributed to the failure of the shoring system. He also pointed to the age and structural condition of the collapsed building as possible contributing factors. An older structure with weaknesses may be particularly vulnerable to movement in the surrounding soil.What are investigators examining?The collapsed building was a three-storey structure containing four apartments and a commercial unit on the ground floor. New York City's Department of Buildings is investigating the collapse, including the excavation work at the neighbouring property and whether appropriate safety measures were followed. The investigation is expected to examine whether the excavation was properly designed, whether adequate support systems were installed and whether the building's structural condition was monitored during construction.The neighbouring construction site had previously faced regulatory scrutiny. The Associated Press reported that the city issued a stop-work order in March after finding problems with demolition work. Inspectors subsequently found that work had resumed in violation of the order. New York officials have also pointed to a shortage of building inspectors, renewing calls for stronger oversight of construction projects.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A power station built beside Niagara Falls in 1906 stopped generating electricity in 1974; after more than 50 years, construction has begun on a C$350 million plan to turn it into a five-star hotel
articles.summary: For more than half a century, an imposing industrial landmark overlooking the Canadian Horseshoe Falls stood as a reminder of Niagara's remarkable
articles.body: For more than half a century, an imposing industrial landmark overlooking the Canadian Horseshoe Falls stood as a reminder of Niagara's remarkable electricity-generating past. Once responsible for harnessing the power of one of the world's most famous waterfalls, the historic Toronto Power Generating Station is now preparing for an entirely different purpose. After decades of inactivity, the century-old structure is being given a new lease on life through a C$350 million redevelopment that will transform it into Niagara Falls' first five-star hotel.Hydroelectric pioneer to historic siteE.J. Lennox designed the 1906 Toronto Power Generating Station on the upper Niagara River in Beaux-Arts style. According to The Spaces, applying this elaborate architectural style to an industrial facility was unusual at the time, making the building an architectural achievement as well as an engineering milestone.The facility supplied electricity to Toronto before ending its generating operations in February 1974. Its historical and technological importance subsequently earned it National Historic Site designation in 1983. Niagara Parks assumed ownership of the property in 2007, preserving the landmark for future generations.C$350 million investment brings new lifeThe redevelopment has now officially entered its construction phase. According to Niagara Parks, a groundbreaking ceremony was held on November 12, 2026, with project partners and Ontario's Minister of Tourism, Culture and Gaming, Zee Hamid, attending the event.Toronto Power Hotel Inc. is investing more than C$350 million in the ambitious restoration and redevelopment. The partnership brings together Society Developments, which is leading the construction, and Pearle Hospitality, which will manage and operate the property once completed.Deltera Contracting Inc., part of the Tridel Group of Companies, has been appointed general contractor. +VG Architects and MT Planners are also ensuring the redevelopment retains the building's character.New guest experiences, luxury accommodationsThe proposed hotel will introduce Niagara Falls' first five-star accommodation, combining heritage architecture with contemporary hospitality.As outlined by Niagara Parks, the development will feature four to five restaurants, a wellness and social spa, multiple event spaces, an art gallery and a museum. Free indoor and outdoor public viewing areas will also allow visitors to enjoy the spectacular surroundings without necessarily staying at the hotel.The project is anticipated to reach substantial completion in 2029 and is projected to create up to 900 jobs in the region, providing economic opportunities for local residents and businesses.The Spaces have shared the larger vision of redevelopment which includes working with the historic building and adding architectural interventions that complement it. The restoration is intended to preserve the legacy of Lennox's original design while establishing a contemporary destination.Niagara's industrial heritage gets a new chapterThe hotel redevelopment adds another dimension to Niagara Falls' growing heritage tourism offering. Niagara Falls Tourism already highlights the region's historic power-generating facilities through immersive exhibitions, restored machinery and interactive experiences at the Niagara Parks Power Station.Visitors can also explore its remarkable 2,200-foot underground tunnel, located 180 feet beneath the building, before reaching an observation deck overlooking the Niagara River.The Toronto Power Generating Station's transformation now promises to connect this industrial legacy with luxury tourism. What once powered homes and industries will soon welcome travellers, diners and cultural enthusiasts, ensuring that one of Niagara Falls' most recognisable historic structures remains relevant for generations to come.Image Courtesy: Niagara ParksYou use AI every day. articles.title: From odd-even to cloud seeding: Why Delhi's pollution battle remains unfinished
articles.summary: Every winter, Delhi's air turns toxic. Governments change, action plans get revamped and new solutions are announced.
articles.body: Every winter, Delhi's air turns toxic.Governments change, action plans get revamped and new solutions are announced.Yet, the capital continues to battle hazardous air, with residents bearing the health costs of a crisis that refuses to go away.At the time of publishing this article on Saturday (7pm IST), Delhi's average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 367, in the ‘very poor’ category, which had breached the ‘severe’ level on Friday.The latest spike came days after Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in five years.Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) governments introduced separate action plans and announced a range of measures to tackle Delhi's recurring air pollution crisis during their respective tenures. Both failed.So are successive governments fighting pollution at its source, or merely trying to manage the smog after it sets in?2024 vs 2026: What changed in strategy?Rules under AAPWhen AAP was in power in Delhi, its 2024 Winter Action Plan focused on a combination of emergency interventions, dust suppression and monitoring of pollution sources.The 21-point plan, announced in September 2024, included drone surveillance of pollution hotspots, a special task force, anti-dust campaigns at construction sites and the deployment of mechanical road sweepers, water sprinklers and mobile anti-smog guns. The odd-even vehicle scheme was another emergency option used by AAP govt to reduce vehicular emissions if air quality deteriorated further.The AAP government's plan also targeted industrial pollution, open waste burning and stubble burning. It called for stricter monitoring of construction sites, action against polluting industrial units and enforcement of pollution-control norms.A ban on firecrackers was announced ahead of Diwali to prevent a seasonal spike in emissions.Rules under BJPFollowing BJP's victory in the February 2025 assembly elections, the new government under chief minister Rekha Gupta introduced a 25-point Air Pollution Mitigation Plan in June, followed by a separate Winter Action Plan in October 2026.Its strategy placed greater emphasis on enforcement against polluting vehicles, construction dust and industrial emissions. Measures included ANPR cameras to identify overage vehicles, restrictions on certain polluting commercial vehicles, expansion of electric public transport and stricter checks at PUC centres. For dust control, the government announced the deployment of 86 mechanical road sweepers, 300 water sprinklers and 362 anti-smog guns under its winter plan.BJP also attempted cloud seeding in October 2025 as an experimental measure to induce artificial rain and wash pollutants out of the air. However, the two trials conducted on October 28 failed to produce rainfall, with insufficient moisture in the clouds cited as the primary reason.A subsequent trial was also called off because of unfavourable atmospheric conditions.This year, the Supreme Court permitted the use of certified green firecrackers during Diwali under limited hours.Why Delhi keeps chokingWhile emergency interventions such as cloud seeding, smog guns and traffic restrictions are often discussed as possible solutions, environmental experts argue that the problem requires a more sustained, science-led approach. Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalysts, explains why these measures have limited impact and what Delhi needs to address the pollution crisis in the long run.Dahiya said cloud seeding cannot be a reliable solution to Delhi's winter pollution as it requires moisture-laden clouds, which are largely absent during the smog season."You can't seed clouds that aren't there," he said, adding that even if artificial rain is induced, the relief may last only a few hours. Pollution also moves across administrative boundaries and can quickly return due to emissions from the wider Delhi-NCR airshed. "Cloud seeding treats the symptom, at best, for a few hours," he said.On the contribution of vehicles to Delhi's pollution, Dahiya said they remain among the biggest local sources of PM2.5. Citing IITM's real-time data, he said vehicular emissions accounted for 31% of PM2.5 on November 13, making them the largest single direct source. However, he cautioned against relying solely on restrictions without improving public transport."You can't ban your way out if people have no alternative," he said, pointing out that around 6,400 buses with GPS were tracked on Delhi's roads on November 13, below the city's long-standing target.He also questioned the effectiveness of smog guns and water sprinklers in reducing city-wide PM2.5 levels, saying they mainly settle coarse dust over limited areas, while winter pollution is largely driven by fine combustion particles and secondary pollutants.Calling for dust control through paving, covering construction materials and mechanised sweeping, he described spraying water into the air as "visible action, not effective action".Prolonged exposure to toxic airThe impact of Delhi's recurring pollution crisis goes beyond seasonal coughing, breathlessness and respiratory infections. Doctors warn that prolonged exposure to polluted air can affect lung development in children and increase the risk of respiratory and cardiovascular problems.Dr Nikhil Rajvanshi, Consultant – Pediatric Pulmonologist, Allergy and Sleep Specialist, Rainbow Children's Hospital, Delhi, explains that children inhale more air relative to their body weight than adults, making them particularly vulnerable to pollutants. He warns that children exposed to high pollution levels over several years may experience reduced lung growth and lower lung function as adults. Importantly, even children without diagnosed respiratory conditions are not immune. "Some effects may persist even after exposure decreases," he cautions.Highlighting the wider health implications, Dr Vikas Mittal, Director – Pulmonology, CK Birla Hospital, Delhi, says PM2.5 particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, triggering inflammation across the body. Repeated exposure can worsen asthma and COPD, impair lung function and increase cardiovascular risks, including hypertension, heart attacks and strokes. He also warns that prolonged exposure can cause lasting changes to lung tissue, even among otherwise healthy individuals."Some changes may improve when exposure is reduced, but prolonged injury and remodelling of lung tissue may not be completely reversible," he says.The doctors also highlight the potential consequences of continued exposure over the next five to ten years. Dr Rajvanshi warns that an entire generation of children growing up in highly polluted environments could face reduced peak lung function, increased asthma prevalence and greater susceptibility to respiratory infections in adulthood.Dr Mittal cautions that the consequences would not be limited to people with existing illnesses, as otherwise healthy individuals are also vulnerable to the cumulative effects of prolonged exposure.Seasonal firefighting or lasting solutionsWith the crisis extending beyond Delhi's borders, responsibility cannot rest with one government or one agency alone. It requires coordination between the Centre, Delhi and neighbouring states, along with measurable targets and accountability for missed deadlines.As political parties trade claims over who is responsible for the city's deteriorating air, residents continue to breathe the consequences. Ultimately, the success of any government's pollution plan will not be measured by the number of announcements or anti-smog guns deployed, but by whether Delhi can finally breathe easier, not just in winter, but throughout the year.The scale of the challenge, Dahiya said, cannot be understood by looking at Delhi's borders or the winter stubble-burning season alone.He said stubble burning accounts for less than 5% of Delhi's PM2.5 over a full year, while only around 30% of the city's pollution originates within its boundaries. This makes a regional approach essential, rather than one that focuses only on Delhi or relies on measures activated when AQI levels spike.He called for a regional airshed plan covering the NCR and the Indo-Gangetic plain, with year-round emission-reduction targets for vehicles, industries, power plants, waste, household fuel and dust. "We need targets for how many tonnes each source and each geography must cut, and by when," he said.Dr Mittal says the priority must be controlling pollution at its source through stricter checks on vehicular emissions, industrial pollution, construction dust and crop-residue burning."Clean air is a public health necessity, and controlling pollution at its source remains the most effective long-term solution," he says.So, until action moves beyond seasonal restrictions and visible interventions to measurable reductions in emissions, the capital risks returning to the same cycle of toxic air every winter.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: UK barrister Forz Khan suspended over LinkedIn posts calling for ‘global cleansing’ of Zionism
articles.summary: Forz Khan, a UK barrister, faces a four-month suspension for posting anti-Semitic remarks on LinkedIn, calling for the global cleansing of Zionism, with implications for public confidence in the legal profession.
articles.body: A UK barrister has been suspended from practising for four months after a disciplinary panel found that several posts he published on LinkedIn contained anti-Semitic and seriously offensive remarks about Israel and Zionism.Forz Khan, who has worked as a self-employed barrister in London since being called to the Bar in 1988, was found guilty of professional misconduct following a hearing before the Bar Standards Board (BSB). He was also ordered to pay £2,880 in costs, The Telegraph reported.The panel examined a series of statements Khan published on his LinkedIn account, including calls for the global eradication of Zionists and references to a "final solution" to what he described as the problem of Israel.What did the barrister post on LinkedIn?In March last year, Khan wrote that Zionism could only be addressed through a "complete global cleansing", claiming the ideology would otherwise continue to spread hatred and violence.Another post described Israel as an "apartheid war criminal entity" and accused its government and military of committing genocide and violating international law.He also wrote: "The world needs to eradicate Zios globally."In a separate statement, Khan referred to Israel as a recruitment tool for Hamas and said there was "only 1 final solution" to the country.He continued posting similar remarks the following month, writing that the region would remain affected by what he called evil until Israel was completely dismantled.One of his other posts stated: "Scum like this should be in a gas chamber."What did the Bar Standards Board say?The disciplinary panel concluded that Khan's statements, whether considered individually or collectively, amounted to anti-Semitic and seriously offensive conduct in the context in which they were published.In its decision, the panel said his behaviour was likely to undermine public confidence in both him and the legal profession.It stated: "Mr Forz Khan, a barrister, behaved in a manner which was likely to diminish the trust and confidence which the public places in him or in the profession."The panel added that the comments, "taken either together or individually, and in the context in which they were made, were anti-Semitic and/or seriously offensive," according to the news outlet.You use AI every day. articles.title: Walmart outage today: After Microsoft disruption, payroll, HR services affected in 11,500 businesses as Workday goes down
articles.summary: Walmart was one of the 11,500 businesses that locked out their employees as HR platform Workday went down on Friday.
articles.body: Walmart was one of the 11,500 businesses that locked out their employees as HR platform Workday went down on Friday. The website Downdetector first reported nearly 3,000 outage reports for the platform shortly after 5 p.m. Friday. The disruption came just as Microsoft was struggling to restore its own services following a global outage affecting Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 applications.Workday, which provides cloud-based human resources and financial management software to more than 11,500 organisations worldwide, said some customers were experiencing a service disruption. The company temporarily placed production systems into maintenance mode after discovering a problem while testing its disaster-recovery environment."We're working urgently to investigate and resolve the issue," a Workday spokesperson said, apologizing to affected customers.According to a technical notification shared by Washington University IT, Workday discovered that services in its disaster-recovery environment had unexpectedly connected to production databases during routine maintenance validation. This left some data in an inconsistent state, potentially causing errors when users attempted to access their accounts or execute jobs, integrations and other tasks.The company said it was investigating the best recovery path and planned to provide updates every 30 minutes.Who was affected by the Workday outage?The disruption affected customers across multiple sectors, including universities and businesses. Washington University, Brown University, Emerson College, Georgia Tech and Saint Joseph's University were among the institutions that reported Workday-related service problems.At Brown University, employees were advised that regular Workday functions, including time reporting, benefits enrolment, expense reports, hiring activities and leave management, were unavailable. Staff were asked to maintain separate records of their working hours so the information could be entered once the platform was restored.Workday is used by organisations for payroll processing, recruitment, employee benefits, attendance tracking, leave requests and other administrative functions. Its customers include major companies such as Walmart, Target and Nordstrom, although there was no confirmed indication that all or any of these retailers were affected by Friday's incident.The company has not disclosed the total number of customers or employees affected by the disruption.Walmart, Target, ChipotleCorporate giants like Walmart, Target, General Electric, Morgan Stanley, Netflix and Southwest Airlines all use Workday. articles.title: 'We'll be kingmakers in UP polls': Chandrashekhar Azad bets big on tie-up with Asaduddin Owaisi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Chandrashekhar Azad had dropped ‘Ravan’ from his name a while ago, fearing religious politics would portray him as \"anti-Ram\".
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chandrashekhar Azad had dropped ‘Ravan’ from his name a while ago, fearing religious politics would portray him as "anti-Ram". Speaking to TOI days after announcing a tie-up with AIMIM's Asaduddin Owaisi, the Nagina MP and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief said the same calculation led him to become the Samajik Parivartan Morcha’s CM face, "denying BJP an 80:20 polarisation weapon".He said, “A Dalit CM face will not give BJP an opportunity to polarise the election and derail our larger objective of removing it from power.”The alliance’s wager is Dalit-Muslim unity. Citing the 2011 Census, he put the Scheduled Caste population at 21% and Muslims at 18-19% in UP. With no 2021 Census, he estimated their combined share at 45%, "influencing 275 of UP’s 403 seats".Azad said: “In politics, one and one make 11. Why should we not try to form our own govt?” Rejecting the ‘vote-katua’ (vote cutter) tag, he cited his 51%-plus victory in Nagina in the previous Lok Sabha polls. “Don't worry about me; worry about the people of UP,” he said, adding, "Those dismissing this alliance will see us emerge as kingmakers in UP."Without the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), the SP will not repeat its western UP performance, Azad said, pointing to RLD’s eight regional seats in 2022 before it joined the NDA in 2024. He cited the December 2022 Khatauli bypoll, won by an RLD-SP-ASP-backed candidate after earlier attempts to wrest the seat had failed, as proof of “unity’s potential”.The Owaisi-Azad alliance followed "15 days of opposition talks". Azad alleged that senior opposition leaders felt they did not need smaller allies, despite failing since 2017 to translate their support into power. He cited the BJP’s accommodation of Om Prakash Rajbhar, Dara Singh Chauhan and Keshav Prasad Maurya despite past disagreements or defeats.He also questioned the opposition’s response to EVM manipulation and vote-theft allegations: “Which of their leaders went to jail, faced bullets or lathi-charges, or had their homes burnt?” he asked, referring to the protests and crackdowns faced by his cadre and the Muslim community.During the anti-CAA/NRC protests, he said, he spent about a month in jail and continued protesting despite intelligence warnings, facing pellet guns and sitting through multiple spells of rain.For Azad, the Owaisi partnership is personal too. When a video of Azad at the recent NEET protests went viral, Owaisi visited the Dalit leader, asked whether he had eaten and urged him to look after himself. “That day, I developed deep respect for him,” Azad said, praising Owaisi’s command of parliamentary debates, constitutional rights and the concerns of marginalised communities.The Morcha’s agenda includes free, common education till Class 12 and a law requiring everyone drawing a government salary, using a government facility or receiving a government pension — from DMs and secretaries to legislators and teachers — to send their children to government schools. He said lawmakers must experience the public education system and improve school buildings, water supply, hygiene, teaching and resources. “When the children of lawmakers and officials study in these schools, the infrastructure, hygiene and teaching standards will automatically improve,” he said.Azad promised the maximum share of the state GDP for education and healthcare, "filling four to five lakh vacancies", particularly reservation backlogs for SCs, STs and OBCs, and investment in rural industries to curb migration. His agenda includes guaranteed MSP, tackling urea and DAP shortages, clearing sugarcane mill dues and developing rural sports.He said the campaign would rely neither on corporate money nor on elaborate media machinery. Invoking BR Ambedkar’s belief that “a man can go hungry, but not without respect”, he said Kanshi Ram built a national party through cadre and word of mouth. "Social media offers millions of viewers now."The Morcha's first show of strength will be a November 26 Constitution Day rally in Lucknow, with the slogan “Neela-hara jhanda saath chalega, Samvidhan saath chalega” (Blue and green flags will come together, taking our Constitution along).You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Trump considers holding back on Iran strikes even as military keeps options open
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump is considering holding back from renewed military strikes against Iran, provided Tehran and its regional allies do not trigger
articles.body: US president Donald Trump is considering holding back from renewed military strikes against Iran, provided Tehran and its regional allies do not trigger further escalation, according to a Reuters report citing people familiar with his discussions with senior advisers.Trump has discussed the possibility of avoiding fresh attacks during national security meetings and intelligence briefings in recent days, the report said. His position, however, remains uncertain, with the president having alternated between threatening a wider military campaign and signalling that he wants to bring the conflict to an end.The shift comes as US allies in the region press Washington to avoid returning to full-scale hostilities. Trump has also acknowledged their concerns, saying in an interview with sports broadcaster Stephen A Smith on Thursday that he could end the conflict immediately but was extending the process at the request of countries he wanted to protect.The war, launched by the US and Israel in February, has driven up global fuel prices and become a political liability for Trump's administration. A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted shortly before the November 3 midterm elections found that 55% of Americans believed the war was not worth its cost. The Republicans subsequently lost control of Congress to the Democrats.A White House official said Trump remained the sole decision-maker on military action and that the US was in a strong position, citing its control of the Strait of Hormuz and what it described as a collapsing Iranian economy.Saudi Arabia, Turkey urge restraintTrump has sought the views of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish president Tayyip Erdogan in telephone conversations over the past two weeks. Both leaders advised him against restarting attacks on Iran, according to people familiar with the discussions. Trump did not commit to either course of action, the report said.During a conversation with bin Salman on October 31, Trump reportedly said he was planning to attack Iran after the US elections. The Saudi crown prince urged him to reconsider, arguing that economic sanctions were already putting pressure on Tehran.Erdogan has also spoken with Trump three times since October 28. A Turkish presidential statement following their November 7 conversation emphasised the need to resolve tensions between Washington and Tehran.US intelligence assessments suggest that the naval blockade and economic sanctions are damaging Iran's economy and could continue to exert pressure on the country, according to US officials cited by Reuters.The US military has also been working to restrict the movement of weapons and other sanctioned goods into Iran by land and through the Caspian Sea, extending a blockade that has already targeted Iranian maritime traffic.US military keeps options openDespite the diplomatic push to avoid renewed fighting, the US military is prepared to escalate if Trump orders it to do so, according to people familiar with military planning.A third aircraft carrier is expected to move into the Middle East in the coming days to replace one of the two currently operating in the region. All three could remain deployed if required, the sources said.One option discussed by Trump is another strike on Iran's underground nuclear facilities. However, the US has already attacked those sites, and the effectiveness of a further bombing campaign remains uncertain.US intelligence assessments have also indicated that renewed strikes are unlikely to significantly alter Iran's negotiating demands, two US officials told Reuters.While regional partners are urging restraint, Israeli officials have continued to lobby the Trump administration for another military campaign against Iran, according to a US official cited in the report.Trump has suggested that Washington may have exhausted the possibilities of negotiations with Tehran, but has not announced whether he intends to resume military operations.You use AI every day. articles.title: D'sthala villagers seek action against rumour-mongers
articles.summary: Dharmasthala villagers demand legal action against activists over false claims of 1,510 unnatural deaths, citing RTI data showing 374; seek justice in rape-murder case.
articles.body: Mangaluru: Villagers of Dharmasthala have sought legal action against activists who allegedly spread false information claiming that 1,510 unnatural deaths occurred in the village. Dharmasthala GP former vice-president Srinivas Rao said RTI replies showed that 374 unnatural deaths had been reported. He said the figure of 1,510 deaths (between 2000 and 2014) cited by activists relates to the entire Belthangady taluk covering 81 villages, and not Dharmasthala alone. "We demand legal action against those spreading false information. Lakhs of devotees visit Sri Kshetra Dharmasthala every year.,” Rao told reporters on Saturday. He said villagers unanimously sought justice for the 17-year-old girl who was raped and murdered.Stay updated with the latest Mangaluru news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Gangster brought to Malpe to attend mother’s funeral
articles.summary: Gangster Ravi Pujari brought to Malpe under tight security to attend mother’s funeral after court permission; extradited from Senegal after 25 years.
articles.body: Udupi: Gangster Ravi Pujari was brought to Malpe under tight police security on Saturday to attend the funeral of his mother, who died on Thursday night. Sushila Poojarthi, 86, reportedly passed away at her house. The funeral was held at the family’s ancestral house in Nergi, Malpe, on Saturday.Following the death, Ravi Pujari had approached the court seeking permission to attend her last rites. Udupi SP Hariram Shankar confirmed that a court has granted permission to Ravi to attend the funeral. Security arrangements were handled by Bengaluru prison authorities, with additional support from Udupi Police, he said.Pujari was extradited from Senegal in west Africa, nearly 25 years after he left the country.Stay updated with the latest Mangaluru news.
